choices: Essentially pronominal verb: agrees with the subject
Se is an indirect object: no agreement
Direct object placed before avoir: agrees
questions.explanation: Each ending follows from one question: which auxiliary, and is there a direct object before the verb? Impersonal verbs, en and indirect se all leave the participle unchanged.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in careful written French? Select all that apply.
choices: Elle s'est rendu compte de son erreur.
La patiente que j'ai soignée va mieux.
questions.explanation: "S'est rendu compte" and "se sont succédé" never agree; "que j'ai soignée" agrees with que = la patiente. "S'est lavée les mains" should be "lavé" (the object, les mains, comes after), and "ont opérés" should be "opéré" (no direct object before avoir).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "The GP I saw reassured me." (The speaker is a woman.)
questions.explanation: "La généraliste que j'ai consultée m'a rassurée." Consultée agrees with que (= la généraliste); rassurée agrees with m' (the speaker, a woman), a direct object placed before avoir.

questions.stem: Name the numbered people and things.

image.alt: Two panels. Left, Au cabinet médical: a doctor in a white coat with a stethoscope behind a desk with a sheet of paper, and a person on a chair. Right, À l'hôpital: a man in blue scrubs, cap and mask; a person lying in a hospital bed; a woman in a white uniform next to a drip stand. Five items are numbered.

questions.explanation: In the surgery, the GP (le généraliste) has written a prescription (l'ordonnance). In the hospital, the man in scrubs is the surgeon (le chirurgien), the person in bed is the patient, and the woman by the drip is the nurse (l'infirmière).

questions.stem: "D'ici 2030, la commune ___ une deuxième maison de retraite."
questions.explanation: D'ici + a future date: the futur antérieur says what will be done by then. "Aurait ouvert" is a conditionnel passé, and "ouvrait" and "avait ouvert" are past tenses.

questions.stem: "Mamie ne répond pas ? Elle ___ son portable." (a guess about why)
questions.explanation: The futur antérieur can guess about the past: "Elle aura oublié son portable" = she must have forgotten her phone (= elle a dû oublier). The other forms don't express a guess about something already done.

questions.stem: "Il n'est pas encore là ? Il aura raté son train." What does it mean?
choices: He would have missed his train.
He must have missed his train.
questions.explanation: Here the futur antérieur is a guess about the past, like "il a dû rater son train". "He will miss" would be "il ratera"; "he would have missed" would be "il aurait raté".

questions.stem: When would someone say "On aura tout essayé !"?
choices: When nothing they tried has worked
When they plan to try everything next year
questions.explanation: The futur antérieur can look back on a whole period, as if from its end: "We'll have tried everything", said when all attempts have failed.

questions.stem: "En 1990, Martine savait déjà qu'elle ___ sa retraite à soixante ans." (She retired long ago.)
questions.explanation: A future seen from a past moment takes the conditionnel présent: "savait … qu'elle prendrait". "Prendra" would look ahead from today, but her retirement is long past; "prenne" is a subjunctive, which savoir que doesn't take; "aura pris" is a futur antérieur, which can't follow a past main verb here.

questions.stem: "En 2019, le maire avait promis que les travaux ___ avant l'hiver suivant."
questions.explanation: After a past verb of promising, the futur moves to the conditionnel: "seront finis" becomes "seraient finis". "Étaient finis" would say the work was already done; the subjunctive is not used after promettre que.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a futur antérieur?
choices: J'aurais fini plus tôt sans toi.
questions.explanation: "J'aurai fini" (without s) is the futur antérieur: finished by tomorrow noon. "J'aurais fini" is the conditionnel passé, used in the other three: an unreal past, the future in the past, and a regret.

questions.stem: "Ne t'inquiète pas : ma mère sera ___ avant nous."
questions.explanation: Rentrer takes être, so the participle agrees with the subject, ma mère: "sera rentrée".

questions.stem: In careful French: "Quand vous ___ le dossier, envoyez-le à votre caisse de retraite."
questions.explanation: The filling-in comes first and is still in the future: careful French uses the futur antérieur after quand. "Remplissez" would suggest at the same time; "auriez rempli" and "aviez rempli" don't fit an instruction about the future.

questions.stem: According to the reading, what happened in France in 2025 for the first time since the end of the Second World War?
choices: There were more deaths than births.
questions.explanation: "La France a compté plus de décès (environ 651 000) que de naissances (environ 645 000)." Life expectancy, in fact, rose.

questions.stem: In the reading, what is the life expectancy at birth of women in 2025?
questions.explanation: 85.9 years for women and 80.3 for men. 22.2 is the percentage of people aged 65 or over; 75 is an age group.

questions.stem: "Les communes qui auront anticipé s'en sortiront mieux." Why "auront anticipé"?
choices: It is a guess about the past.
It is a future in the past.
The planning will be done before they cope better.
questions.explanation: Two future actions in order: first the towns plan ahead (futur antérieur), then they cope better (futur simple).

questions.stem: Last month, Paul said he would call me once he had finished. "Le mois dernier, Paul a dit qu'il m'appellerait quand il ___."
questions.explanation: He said: "Je t'appellerai quand j'aurai fini." Seen from the past, the futur becomes a conditionnel présent (appellerait) and the futur antérieur a conditionnel passé (aurait fini).

questions.stem: Which word means a person who looks after an older or dependent relative?
questions.explanation: L'aidant (feminine l'aidante) is a carer. L'actif is a person in the labour force, le retraité a retired person, and le senior an older person.

questions.stem: What is "le taux de natalité"?
questions.explanation: La natalité concerns births, and le taux is a rate. The death rate is le taux de mortalité; life expectancy is l'espérance de vie.

questions.stem: Write the futur antérieur of rembourser: "Dans dix ans, nous ___ la maison."
questions.explanation: Futur of avoir + participle: "nous aurons remboursé": finished by a point in the future.

questions.stem: Use the futur antérieur of se tromper to make a guess: "Mes sœurs ne sont pas encore là : elles ___ de route."
questions.explanation: A guess about the past: "elles se seront trompées de route" (= elles ont dû se tromper). Se tromper is pronominal, so être, and the participle agrees with elles.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the use of the futur antérieur it shows.
left: Il n'est pas là : il aura raté son train.
Quand tu auras mangé, on partira.
Ce siècle aura été celui de la longévité.
choices: Looking back on a whole period
A future seen from the past
questions.explanation: These are the four uses. A future seen from the past uses the conditionnel, not the futur antérieur.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "She knew she would retire at sixty."
questions.explanation: "Elle savait qu'elle prendrait sa retraite à soixante ans." After the past verb savait, the future becomes the conditionnel présent.

questions.stem: Which sentences contain a futur antérieur? Select all that apply.
choices: Dès que j'aurai reçu ma pension, je voyagerai.
questions.explanation: "Aurai reçu", "aura oublié" and "se seront perdues" are futur + participle. "Il aura quatre-vingts ans" is the plain futur of avoir (he will be 80), and "partirait" is a conditionnel présent.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this population pyramid.

image.alt: A simplified population pyramid with invented figures, in ten-year age groups from 0–9 at the bottom to 90+ at the top. Bars on the left and on the right; the 70–79 bars are highlighted; a bracket on the right groups the four top age groups, from 60–69 up. Four parts are numbered.

questions.explanation: Men are on the left and women on the right; the bracket groups the oldest age groups (les seniors, here 60 and over); a single bar such as the 70–79 one is une tranche d'âge (an age group).

questions.stem: "Il fallait qu'il fût présent." What is "fût"?
questions.explanation: After "il fallait que", with a circumflex: the imperfect subjunctive of être. The passé simple "il fut" has no circumflex; faire gives "il fit".

questions.stem: How would you write "Il fallait qu'il partît" in today's French?
questions.explanation: The imperfect subjunctive is read as a present subjunctive: "qu'il parte". "Qu'il soit parti" would be the modern form of a pluperfect subjunctive (qu'il fût parti).

questions.stem: How would you write "Je doutais qu'il eût compris" in today's French?
questions.explanation: "Eût compris" is a pluperfect subjunctive (an earlier action); today the subjonctif passé does the job: "qu'il ait compris".

questions.stem: "J'eusse aimé le connaître." What does it mean?
choices: I would love to know him.
I would have liked to know him.
questions.explanation: "J'eusse aimé" is the conditionnel passé deuxième forme = "j'aurais aimé": I would have liked to.

questions.stem: In which sentence is "eût" or "eut" a passé simple?
choices: Il fallait qu'il eût terminé avant midi.
Il eût fallu partir plus tôt.
Bien qu'il eût tort, il insista.
questions.explanation: "Il eut froid" has no circumflex and tells an event in a chain of passé simple verbs (eut … rentra). The other three have eût: a pluperfect subjunctive, a conditionnel passé deuxième forme, and an imperfect subjunctive after bien que.

questions.stem: "Passe me voir, ne fût-ce que cinq minutes." What does "ne fût-ce que" mean?
questions.explanation: Ne fût-ce que is a set phrase still used today: "even if only", "even just". Come and see me, even just for five minutes.

questions.stem: "S'il eût parlé, on l'eût cru." Which modern sentence means the same?
choices: S'il a parlé, on l'a cru.
S'il avait parlé, on l'aurait cru.
questions.explanation: In a literary past hypothesis, the pluperfect subjunctive can stand for both the plus-que-parfait (s'il avait parlé) and the conditionnel passé (on l'aurait cru).

questions.stem: "Eût-il été riche, il n'aurait rien changé." What does the first part mean?
choices: Even if he had been rich
questions.explanation: Inverted, the pluperfect subjunctive means "even if": eût-il été riche = même s'il avait été riche.

questions.stem: Where are you most likely to meet "qu'il vînt"?
questions.explanation: The imperfect subjunctive belongs to literary prose, especially before the mid-20th century. Everyday French says "qu'il vienne".

questions.stem: In classical prose, which subjunctive follows "Je voulais que …" for an action at the same time or later?
questions.explanation: The classical concordance des temps put the imperfect subjunctive after a past main verb: "Je voulais qu'il vînt". Modern French uses the present subjunctive: "qu'il vienne".

questions.stem: In French, a formal, careful register of language is called le registre ___.
questions.explanation: Le registre soutenu (la langue soutenue) is the formal register. Désuet means old-fashioned, archaïque archaic, and naguère is an adverb (not long ago).

questions.stem: What is "un recueil de nouvelles"?
questions.explanation: Un recueil is a collection (of poems or stories), and une nouvelle here is a short story. An extract is un extrait.

questions.stem: Match each classical form to the form you would use today.
questions.explanation: Imperfect subjunctive → present subjunctive (vînt → vienne, eût → ait, fît → fasse); pluperfect subjunctive → past subjunctive (fût venu → soit venu).

questions.stem: Which are imperfect subjunctive forms? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Parlât, finît and fût carry the circumflex of the imperfect subjunctive (and follow que). "Il parla" and "il fut" are passé simple.

questions.stem: Rewrite in today's French: "Il fallait qu'elle vînt." → Il fallait qu'elle ___.
questions.explanation: Imperfect subjunctive → present subjunctive: "qu'elle vienne".

questions.stem: Rewrite in today's French: "Il eût fallu partir." → Il ___ ___ partir.
questions.explanation: "Il eût fallu" is the conditionnel passé deuxième forme: today, "il aurait fallu partir" (we should have left).

questions.stem: Where and when was Saint-Exupéry born?
questions.explanation: "Antoine de Saint-Exupéry naquit à Lyon le 29 juin 1900." Toulouse was the start of the airmail line; Marseille is where his wreck was found.

questions.stem: What was his job at Cap Juby in 1927?
choices: Station manager on the edge of the desert
questions.explanation: "On le nomma chef d'escale à Cap Juby": station manager. He ran the Aeroposta Argentina from 1929.

questions.stem: Which book won the prix Femina in 1931?
questions.explanation: Vol de nuit, inspired by night flights in South America, won the prix Femina in 1931. Courrier sud came out in 1929, Terre des hommes in 1939 and Le Petit Prince in 1943.

questions.stem: What happened on 30 December 1935?
choices: He took off from Corsica for the last time.
His plane crashed in the Libyan desert during a record attempt.
questions.explanation: During a Paris–Saigon record attempt, he and his mechanic André Prévot crashed in the Libyan desert; a Bedouin found them after several days. His last flight was on 31 July 1944.

questions.stem: Which is the usual spoken version of "À peine son livre était-il paru qu'il partit pour l'Amérique du Sud"?
choices: Son livre était à peine paru qu'il est parti pour l'Amérique du Sud.
À peine son livre paraissait qu'il partait pour l'Amérique du Sud.
Son livre avait à peine paru qu'il partira pour l'Amérique du Sud.
Son livre était à peine paru qu'il soit parti pour l'Amérique du Sud.
questions.explanation: In speech: no inversion, à peine after the auxiliary, and the passé composé for the second event. The other versions change the tenses or use a subjunctive, which à peine … que doesn't take.

questions.stem: "Le pilote vit le sable, coupa le moteur et atterrit." What is "atterrit"?
questions.explanation: For finir-type verbs, the il form of the present and of the passé simple are the same (il atterrit). In a chain of passé simple verbs (vit, coupa), it is the passé simple: in speech, "il a atterri".

questions.stem: In a DELF oral, which is the best way to present Le Petit Prince?
choices: Recite its most famous sentence from memory.
Give the date and genre, sum up the story in your own words, and name its themes.
Say only that you liked it.
questions.explanation: Facts, a summary in your own words and the themes are what an examiner wants; a quotation from memory risks being wrong and shows nothing of your French.

questions.stem: What do we know today about the cause of his last crash?
choices: It was certainly an engine failure.
He was shot down over Corsica.
He ran out of fuel over the Sahara.
questions.explanation: "On ignore encore aujourd'hui ce qui provoqua l'accident." Several hypotheses circulate, but none has been proved. The wreck lies off Marseille, not Corsica or the Sahara.

questions.stem: Put these events of Saint-Exupéry's life in order.
choices: Il entra dans la compagnie de Pierre Latécoère.
Il fut chef d'escale à Cap Juby.
Son avion s'écrasa dans le désert de Libye.
Il publia Le Petit Prince à New York.
Il décolla de Borgo pour sa dernière mission.
questions.explanation: 1900 Lyon; 1926 Latécoère; 1927 Cap Juby; 1929 Buenos Aires; December 1935 the desert crash; 1943 Le Petit Prince; 31 July 1944 the last flight.

questions.stem: Match each book to the year it came out.
questions.explanation: Courrier sud (1929) was written at Cap Juby; Vol de nuit (1931) won the prix Femina; Terre des hommes (1939) tells, among other things, the 1935 crash; Le Petit Prince came out in New York in 1943. He joined Latécoère in 1926 and disappeared in 1944.

questions.stem: Name the numbered stops on this simplified map of the airmail line.

image.alt: A simplified map of south-western Europe, north-west Africa and South America with the Atlantic Ocean between them. A dashed red route joins six dots: one in France, three down the African coast, one on the Brazilian coast and one further south. Five dots are numbered.

questions.explanation: The line started in Toulouse, ran down the African coast through Casablanca (the unnumbered dot) and Cap Juby to Dakar, crossed the South Atlantic to Natal in Brazil, and went on to Buenos Aires.

questions.stem: Retell in the passé composé: "L'avion décolla à six heures." → L'avion ___ à six heures.
questions.explanation: Décoller takes avoir: "l'avion a décollé".

questions.stem: Which statements are true according to the lesson? Select all that apply.
choices: The wreck of his plane was identified in 2004.
A fisherman found his silver bracelet in 1998.
Le Petit Prince was first published in Paris.
He flew his last mission from Toulouse.
Terre des hommes tells the story of the 1935 desert crash.
questions.explanation: The bracelet was found in 1998 near Marseille and the wreck identified in 2004; Terre des hommes (1939) tells the desert crash. Le Petit Prince first came out in New York, and his last mission took off from Borgo in Corsica.

questions.stem: Which word is "the wreck" of a ship or a plane?
questions.explanation: L'épave is the wreck. L'atterrissage is the landing, la traversée the crossing, and le décollage the take-off.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je suis content que tu ___ ton examen hier." (réussir)
questions.explanation: Être content que takes the subjunctive, and "hier" puts the success before the feeling: subjonctif passé, que tu aies réussi. "As réussi" and "avais réussi" are indicative; "réussisses" is the present subjunctive, for something at the same time or later.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je suis soulagée que mes sœurs ___ bien ___." (arriver)
questions.explanation: Arriver takes être, so the subjonctif passé is soient arrivé(e)s, and with être the participle agrees with the subject: mes sœurs is feminine plural, so arrivées. "Arrivés" has the wrong gender, "aient arrivé" the wrong auxiliary, and "sont" is the indicative.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il faut que nous ___ fini l'échauffement avant midi."
questions.explanation: The subjunctive of avoir for nous is "ayons", with no i after the y (likewise "ayez"). "Ayions" is a common misspelling; "avons" is the indicative present and "aurons" the futur.

questions.stem: Complete: "Nous sommes ravis que vous ___ dimanche prochain." (venir)
questions.explanation: "Dimanche prochain" is later than the main verb, so the present subjunctive: que vous veniez (from the nous imparfait, nous venions). "Soyez venus" would place the coming before the joy; "venez" and "viendrez" are indicative, but être ravi que needs the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm sorry you were ill"?
choices: Je suis désolé que tu aies été malade.
Je suis désolé que tu sois malade.
Je suis désolé d'avoir été malade.
Je suis désolé que tu étais malade.
questions.explanation: The illness is over before the feeling and there are two subjects: subjonctif passé, que tu aies été malade. "Que tu sois malade" means you are ill now; "d'avoir été malade" means I was ill; "que tu étais" uses the indicative after a feeling.

questions.stem: "She is proud to have run the Paris marathon." Complete: "Elle est fière ___ le marathon de Paris."
questions.explanation: One subject (she is proud, she ran), so French uses a past infinitive: être fière d'avoir couru. "Qu'elle ait couru" would need a second person; "qu'elle a couru" is the indicative; "courue" adds an agreement that avoir doesn't take here.

questions.stem: In standard written French, complete: "Je ne pense pas que les joueurs ___."  (se tromper, in the past)
questions.explanation: In careful French a negative "penser" takes the subjunctive; the mistake is over, so subjonctif passé. Pronominal verbs take être, and here se is the direct object, so the participle agrees: se soient trompés. "Se sont trompés" is the indicative (heard in casual speech); "trompé" lacks agreement; pronominal verbs never take avoir.

questions.stem: What does "Partons avant qu'il ne soit trop tard" mean?
choices: Let's leave before it isn't too late.
Let's not leave until it's too late.
Let's leave: it isn't too late.
Let's leave before it's too late.
questions.explanation: The ne after avant que is a ne explétif: it has no negative meaning and is optional in careful French. A real negative would need pas. So the sentence simply means "before it's too late".

questions.stem: In standard written French, complete: "Bien qu'elle ___ la finale, elle a battu son record."  (perdre)
questions.explanation: Bien que takes the subjunctive in standard French, and losing the final came before: qu'elle ait perdu. "A perdu" and "avait perdu" are indicative (heard in casual speech, not in careful writing); "aie" is the je form of avoir.

questions.stem: In standard written French, complete: "Ces médailles ? Je ne crois pas qu'elle les ___ toutes ___."  (remporter)
questions.explanation: Ne pas croire takes the subjunctive: qu'elle ait remporté. Remporter uses avoir, and the direct object les (= ces médailles, feminine plural) comes before it, so the participle agrees: remportées. Without agreement ("remporté") the rule is broken; "a" is indicative (casual speech only); remporter doesn't take être.

questions.stem: Which word names the exercises you do just before training or a race?
questions.explanation: L'échauffement is the warm-up (s'échauffer = to warm up). L'entraînement is training itself, l'endurance is stamina and un exploit is a feat.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le coureur a été suspendu deux ans pour ___."
questions.explanation: Suspendu pour dopage: suspended for doping. Un record, le classement (the rankings) and un supporter (a fan) don't fit a reason for a ban.

questions.stem: Write the subjonctif passé of partir (two words): "Je regrette qu'elle ___ si tôt hier soir."
questions.explanation: Partir takes être, so the subjunctive of être + the participle, agreeing with elle: qu'elle soit partie.

questions.stem: Write the subjonctif passé of finir (two words), for something that must be complete by a set time: "Il faut que vous ___ avant 14 heures."
questions.explanation: Finished before a point in the future: subjonctif passé, que vous ayez fini (avoir in the subjunctive: ayez, with no i).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I'm delighted that our team has qualified."
questions.explanation: Je suis ravi que notre équipe se soit qualifiée. Être ravi que + subjunctive; se qualifier takes être, and the participle agrees with l'équipe (feminine singular).

questions.stem: Match each verb with its subjonctif passé for il.
questions.explanation: Arriver and naître take être; se blesser is pronominal, so être too; remporter takes avoir. "Qu'il ait arrivé" uses the wrong auxiliary and "qu'il est né" is the indicative.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in standard French? Select all that apply.
choices: Je suis contente que tu sois venue.
Il est parti sans que je l'aie vu.
Je suis content que j'aie gagné.
questions.explanation: "Que tu sois venue" and "sans que je l'aie vu" are correct subjonctifs passés. Douter que needs the subjunctive (qu'il ait gagné). With one subject, use the past infinitive: je suis content d'avoir gagné.

questions.stem: Name the numbered people and things in the stadium.

image.alt: A stadium scene with six numbered markers: the crowd in the stand, an athlete on the second step of a podium, a gold medal on the winner, the podium itself, a referee in black with a whistle, and a coach in a purple tracksuit holding a stopwatch.

questions.explanation: The crowd are les supporters; each athlete on the podium is un athlète or une athlète; the winner wears la médaille d'or; l'arbitre has the whistle; l'entraîneur holds the stopwatch.

questions.stem: In careful written French, complete: "Nous cherchons un appartement qui ___ un balcon."
questions.explanation: The flat is looked for and may not exist, so careful French uses the subjunctive: qui ait un balcon. "Qui a un balcon" is common in speech but presents the flat as real. "Aie" is the je form; "avait" is the imparfait.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ça y est, j'ai trouvé un appartement qui ___ calme !"
questions.explanation: You have found the flat: the antecedent is real and identified, so the indicative: qui est calme. "Soit" would treat it as something still hoped for; "sois" is the je / tu form; "serait" would make it hypothetical.

questions.stem: In careful written French, complete: "Il n'y a personne ici qui ___ nous aider."
questions.explanation: A denied antecedent (personne) takes the subjunctive in careful French: qui puisse. "Qui peut" is heard in casual speech. "Puissent" is plural, but personne is singular.

questions.stem: Which statement about these two sentences is right? "C'est le plus bel appartement que nous ayons visité." / "C'est le plus bel appartement que nous avons visité."
choices: Only the subjunctive is correct after a superlative.
Both are correct; the subjunctive is the usual written choice.
Only the indicative is correct, because the visit really happened.
Both are wrong: a superlative needs the conditionnel.
questions.explanation: After a superlative the subjunctive is usual, presenting the claim as the speaker's judgment; the indicative is also correct and presents a plain fact. Neither is a mistake, and nothing calls for the conditionnel.

questions.stem: What does the subjunctive suggest in "Je cherche une colocataire qui sache cuisiner"?
choices: You know a particular person who can cook.
The person used to know how to cook.
You don't yet know whether such a person exists.
You are ordering someone to learn to cook.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive in the relative clause marks the antecedent as wished for, not yet identified. To talk about a real person you have in mind, French uses the indicative: une colocataire qui sait cuisiner.

questions.stem: Complete with the subjunctive: "C'est la plus petite surface habitable que nous ___."  (voir)
questions.explanation: Superlative + subjonctif passé (the seeing came before): que nous ayons vu. Que stands for la surface, a feminine direct object placed before avoir, so the participle agrees: vue. "Vu" misses the agreement, "ayions" is misspelt, and voir doesn't take être.

questions.stem: In careful written French, complete: "Je ne connais aucun notaire qui ___ libre le samedi."
questions.explanation: Aucun denies the antecedent, so careful French uses the subjunctive: qui soit libre. "Est" and "sera" are indicative; "sois" is the je / tu form.

questions.stem: The bank asks for "un apport de 10 %". What is l'apport?
choices: the deposit paid when you rent a flat
the buyer's own money put down (down payment)
questions.explanation: L'apport (personnel) is the money the buyer puts in. The rental deposit is la caution; the mortgage is le prêt immobilier; the notary is paid separately.

questions.stem: "Nous avons emménagé le 1er juin." What happened on 1 June?
questions.explanation: Emménager = to move in. Déménager is to move out or move house; être expulsé is to be evicted.

questions.stem: Complete: "La cuisine est un peu ___."  (exigu)
questions.explanation: The feminine of exigu is exiguë (1990 spelling: exigüe), with the diaeresis showing that the u is pronounced. "Exigue" lacks it, "exiguée" adds a wrong ending, and "exigus" is masculine plural.

questions.stem: In the reading, why does the writer say "Pas une seule pièce qui soit vraiment claire !"?
choices: The antecedent is denied (not a single room).
It describes the flat they bought.
It follows a conjunction such as bien que.
questions.explanation: Pas une seule pièce denies that such a room exists, so the relative clause takes the subjunctive. There is no superlative or conjunction, and they didn't buy that flat.

questions.stem: According to the reading, what does the bank require before giving a mortgage?
choices: a down payment of at least 10%
questions.explanation: The text says: la banque exige un apport d'au moins 10 % pour nous accorder un prêt immobilier. The co-ownership and the party wall belong to the house they visited.

questions.stem: In careful written French, write one word: "Nous cherchons un studio qui ___ près du métro."  (être; the studio may not exist)
questions.explanation: Looked for, not yet found: subjunctive present, qui soit près du métro.

questions.stem: In careful written French, write one word: "Il n'y a rien dans cette annonce qui me ___."  (plaire)
questions.explanation: Rien denies the antecedent: subjunctive. Plaire: ils plaisent → qu'il plaise.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "It's the only agency that has replied to our message."
questions.explanation: C'est la seule agence qui ait répondu à notre message. After le seul / la seule the subjunctive is usual; the reply is over, so subjonctif passé.

questions.stem: Match each sentence with the reason for its mood.
left: Je cherche un studio qui soit calme.
Il n'y a personne qui puisse venir.
C'est le meilleur notaire que je connaisse.
J'ai trouvé un studio qui est calme.
questions.explanation: The first three take the subjunctive for three reasons: a wished-for antecedent, a denied one, a superlative. The last uses the indicative because the studio has been found. None of them has a conjunction such as bien que.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in careful written French? Select all that apply.
choices: J'ai acheté une maison qui ait un jardin.
Nous voulons un salon qui soit lumineux.
Il n'existe aucun logement qui soit libre.
C'est le premier acquéreur qui a fait une offre.
questions.explanation: A salon you want and a logement that doesn't exist take the subjunctive. After le premier, the indicative is correct for a plain fact in the order of events (the subjunctive would be too). But the house you bought is real: qui a un jardin, not "ait".

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the plan.

image.alt: A floor plan with six numbered markers: a room with a sofa, an open kitchen with a hob, a room with a double bed, a room with a bath and a basin, a hatched wall along the left edge, and a box under the plan showing 58 m².

questions.explanation: The sofa marks le salon, the hob la cuisine, the bed la chambre, the bath la salle de bains. The hatched wall is shared with the next house: le mur mitoyen. The 58 m² is the total surface habitable.

questions.stem: You want Léa to pass on an instruction to Tom: he is to come and see you after class. Complete: "Dis à Tom qu'il ___ me voir après le cours."
questions.explanation: Dire que + subjunctive gives an order: Dis-lui qu'il vienne. With the indicative ("qu'il vient", "qu'il viendra") the sentence would only report a fact: tell him he is coming. "Venait" is the imparfait.

questions.stem: Complete with the meaning "I realised": "J'ai compris qu'elle ___ redoubler."
questions.explanation: Comprendre que meaning "realise" takes the indicative: j'ai compris qu'elle allait redoubler. "Aille" (subjunctive) would give "find it understandable". "Aillait" and "alle" don't exist.

questions.stem: Complete with the meaning "I find it understandable": "Je comprends que les parents ___ inquiets."
questions.explanation: Comprendre que + subjunctive = find it understandable: que les parents soient inquiets. With "sont" the sentence means "I realise the parents are worried", a different meaning from the one asked for. "Seront" is the futur; "soyent" is a misspelling.

questions.stem: In standard written French, complete: "Que le système ___ injuste, beaucoup de parents le pensent."
questions.explanation: A que-clause placed at the start of the sentence takes the subjunctive, even for a fact: Que le système soit injuste, … Put after the verb, the indicative would return: Beaucoup de parents pensent que le système est injuste.

questions.stem: Complete so that the sentence states a result (he did get it): "Il a révisé tous les soirs, de sorte qu'il ___ son bac avec mention."
questions.explanation: A result that really happened takes the indicative: de sorte qu'il a obtenu son bac. The subjunctive ("obtienne") would turn it into a purpose (he revised so that he would get it), which is correct French but not the meaning asked for; "ait obtenu" would be a purpose already achieved, which doesn't fit either. "Obtenait" (imparfait) would describe a repeated or ongoing action, not one exam result.

questions.stem: Complete: "Parle plus fort, de sorte que tout le monde t'___."
questions.explanation: After an imperative, de sorte que expresses a purpose: subjunctive, que tout le monde t'entende. "Entend" and "entendait" are indicative (result); "entendes" is the tu form, but the subject is tout le monde.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il paraît que la réforme ___ reportée à l'an prochain."
questions.explanation: Il paraît que (apparently, hearsay) takes the indicative: la réforme est reportée. Compare il semble que, which usually takes the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which sentence gives an order?
choices: Le principal a écrit que les élèves sont à l'heure.
Le principal a dit que les élèves étaient à l'heure.
Le principal a écrit que les élèves soient à l'heure.
Le principal a écrit que les élèves seraient à l'heure.
questions.explanation: With écrire que, the subjunctive (soient) turns the sentence into an instruction. The indicative versions (sont, étaient, seraient) report what the head said or wrote was, or would be, the case.

questions.stem: In careful French, complete: "La distance explique que tant d'élèves ___ en retard."
questions.explanation: When a fact accounts for another (cela explique que, la distance explique que), careful French uses the subjunctive: que tant d'élèves soient en retard. A person who explains something (il explique que …) takes the indicative.

questions.stem: Complete: "Personne ne s'attendait à ce que le redoublement ___ supprimé si vite."
questions.explanation: S'attendre à ce que + subjunctive: à ce que le redoublement soit supprimé. The indicative forms don't follow à ce que in standard French.

questions.stem: Complete: "J'espère que tu ___ ton bac."
questions.explanation: Affirmative espérer que takes the indicative, often the futur: j'espère que tu réussiras. Compare souhaiter que + subjunctive: je souhaite que tu réussisses. "Réussisse" is the je / il form; "réussirais" is the conditionnel.

questions.stem: What is "le décrochage scolaire"?
questions.explanation: Décrocher = to drop out, so le décrochage scolaire is leaving school early. Repeating a year is le redoublement, absenteeism is l'absentéisme and a stream is une filière.

questions.stem: A collégien is a pupil at …
questions.explanation: Le collégien, la collégienne: a pupil at the collège, from sixième to troisième. A lycée pupil is un lycéen.

questions.stem: Write one word: "Supposons que le bac ___ supprimé : que se passerait-il ?"  (être)
questions.explanation: Supposons que, imagining a case, takes the subjunctive: supposons que le bac soit supprimé.

questions.stem: Write one word to give an order: "Dites aux élèves qu'ils ___ silence."  (faire)
questions.explanation: Dire que + subjunctive = an order: qu'ils fassent silence (subjunctive of faire: fasse, fasses, fasse, fassions, fassiez, fassent).

questions.stem: Match each construction with its meaning.
questions.explanation: The indicative presents a fact (acknowledged, realised, a result); the subjunctive presents something considered or aimed at (accepted as possible, found understandable). De sorte que + subjunctive would be purpose.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "That he is competent, nobody disputes."
questions.explanation: Qu'il soit compétent, personne ne le conteste. The fronted que-clause takes the subjunctive, and le picks it up in the main clause.

questions.stem: Which sentences use the mood correctly in standard written French? Select all that apply.
choices: Il me semble qu'il a raison.
Qu'il a raison, tout le monde le sait.
Je m'attends à ce qu'il vienne.
questions.explanation: Espérer que and il me semble que take the indicative; s'attendre à ce que takes the subjunctive. A fronted que-clause needs the subjunctive: Qu'il ait raison, tout le monde le sait.

questions.stem: Name the numbered stages and exams of French schooling.

image.alt: A staircase of four unlabelled steps showing ages and class names (about 3 to 6, PS, MS, GS; about 6 to 11, CP to CM2; about 11 to 15, sixième to troisième; about 15 to 18, seconde to terminale), with a certificate at the end of the third and fourth steps, and six numbered markers.

questions.explanation: Maternelle (3 to 6), élémentaire (CP to CM2), collège (sixième to troisième, ending with the brevet), lycée (seconde to terminale, ending with the bac). Le cégep is Québec's college after secondary school.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ soient les difficultés du tournage, le film sortira en mars."
questions.explanation: Quel agrees with the noun after soient: les difficultés is feminine plural, so Quelles que soient. "Quelle" is singular, "Quels" masculine, and "quelque" in one word is the classic spelling mistake.

questions.stem: Which noun fits "Quel que soit ___, le film sera tourné"?
questions.explanation: Quel (masculine singular) and soit (singular) need a masculine singular noun: le budget. La distribution would need quelle; les moyens quels … soient; les cascades quelles … soient.

questions.stem: In standard written French, complete: "Si talentueux qu'il ___, l'acteur ne peut pas sauver ce scénario."
questions.explanation: Si + adjective + que is a concessive construction and takes the subjunctive: si talentueux qu'il soit (however talented he may be).

questions.stem: Complete: "Quand bien même le film ___ un succès, il ne serait pas rentable."
questions.explanation: Quand bien même (even if) takes the conditionnel: quand bien même le film serait un succès. "Est" and "sera" would follow même si; "soit" is a subjunctive, which this conjunction doesn't take.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le scénario est faible. Il n'empêche que les acteurs ___ excellents."
questions.explanation: Il n'empêche que introduces the point you assert, so the indicative: les acteurs sont excellents. "Soient" is a subjunctive, "seraient" a conditionnel, "soyent" a misspelling.

questions.stem: Complete: "Même si le film ___ un peu long, je l'ai beaucoup aimé."
questions.explanation: Même si takes the indicative: même si le film est un peu long. Unlike bien que, it never takes the subjunctive, and in this sense not the conditionnel either.

questions.stem: In standard written French, complete: "Le film est réussi, encore que la fin ___ un peu longue."
questions.explanation: Encore que (formal "although", adding a reservation) takes the subjunctive: encore que la fin soit un peu longue.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: En dépit qu'il pleuve, le tournage a continué.
En dépit il pleut, le tournage a continué.
En dépit de qu'il pleut, le tournage a continué.
En dépit de la pluie, le tournage a continué.
questions.explanation: En dépit de is a preposition, a formal malgré: it takes a noun (en dépit de la pluie). It can't introduce a clause.

questions.stem: What is true of "Tout riche qu'il est, il vit simplement" and "Tout riche qu'il soit, il vit simplement"?
choices: Both are correct; the indicative is the traditional form.
Neither is correct: tout can't be followed by que.
questions.explanation: Tout + adjective + que traditionally takes the indicative, because it concedes a real fact; the subjunctive is now common too. Both are correct.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ tu en penses, ce film est devenu un classique."
questions.explanation: Quoi que in two words means "whatever" and is the object of penser: whatever you think of it. "Quoique" (one word) means "although" and would need a complete clause; "quel que" needs soit + a noun.

questions.stem: A friend says the film was "un navet". What does she mean?
choices: It was a very bad film.
questions.explanation: Un navet (informal, literally a turnip) is a very bad film, a flop. An art-house film is un film d'auteur; a dubbed film is un film doublé.

questions.stem: What is "le montage" of a film?
questions.explanation: Le montage is the editing (monter un film, le monteur). The cast is la distribution, the set le plateau, the dubbing le doublage.

questions.stem: According to the review of "Le Dernier Été", what makes up for the film's weaknesses?
questions.explanation: The review says: Quelles que soient ces faiblesses, l'interprétation emporte tout. The budget is modest, the remake is only a project and the dubbing is a regret.

questions.stem: Write one word: "___ que soient vos raisons, le tournage commence demain."
questions.explanation: Les raisons is feminine plural, so quel agrees: Quelles que soient vos raisons.

questions.stem: Write the verb in the conditionnel: "Quand bien même il ___, on tournerait la scène dehors."  (pleuvoir)
questions.explanation: Quand bien même + conditionnel: quand bien même il pleuvrait (futur stem pleuvr- + -ait).

questions.stem: Put the parts of this review in the order concession, turn, support.
choices: Certes, le film est un peu long,
et le scénario s'égare au milieu.
Il n'empêche que l'interprétation est remarquable :
Lina Haddad, en particulier, est d'une justesse rare.
questions.explanation: Concede first (certes …, and the second half of that sentence), turn with il n'empêche que (+ indicative), then support the point with an example.

questions.stem: Match each construction with what follows it.
questions.explanation: Bien que takes the subjunctive, quand bien même the conditionnel, toujours est-il que the indicative (it asserts your point), en dépit de a noun and avoir beau an infinitive (j'ai beau essayer).

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Quoi que tu dises, je reste jusqu'au générique.
Si drôle qu'il soit, ce film m'ennuie.
Quel que soient les risques, on tourne la cascade.
Même si le film soit long, on reste.
questions.explanation: Quoi que and si … que take the subjunctive: dises, soit. Quel que soit agrees with les risques: quels que soient. Même si takes the indicative: même si le film est long.

questions.stem: Name the numbered people and things on the film set.

image.alt: A film set with five numbered markers: a man in a folding chair with a megaphone, a camera on a tripod, three people standing in a row, a clapperboard on a stool, and a man falling head first towards a mattress beside a fake building front.

questions.explanation: The man with the megaphone in the folding chair directs (le réalisateur); the camera is on its tripod; the people waiting in a row are les figurants (extras); the clapperboard is le clap; the man doing the fall is le cascadeur.

questions.stem: Which form does the norm recommend? "Après qu'il ___ parti, nous avons fermé la salle."
questions.explanation: The Académie and the OQLF keep the indicative after après que: après qu'il est parti. "Soit" is very common but criticised; "ait" and "a" use the wrong auxiliary for partir.

questions.stem: Which use of "malgré que" does the Académie française accept?
choices: malgré qu'il pleuve (although it is raining)
malgré qu'il en ait (in spite of himself)
questions.explanation: The Académie advises against malgré que meaning "although" and accepts it only in the old literary phrase malgré qu'il en ait. For "although", write bien que or quoique.

questions.stem: Which sentence does the OQLF accept as standard?
choices: Je me rappelle de cette soirée.
Je m'en rappelle, de ce film.
questions.explanation: Se rappeler normally takes a direct object (je me rappelle cette soirée), but de is accepted before a personal pronoun, because "je me rappelle vous" is impossible. The other three put de (or en) before a thing, which is common but not the norm.

questions.stem: Which is the normative construction?
choices: pallier sur le manque de personnel
questions.explanation: Pallier takes a direct object: pallier un manque. "Pallier à" is very common, by analogy with remédier à, but the Académie condemns it.

questions.stem: Which version follows the norm? "Parle lentement, ___"
choices: de façon à ce qu'on te comprenne.
de façon à ce qu'on te comprend.
questions.explanation: For purpose, the norm is de façon que + subjunctive. De façon à ce que is very common and recorded in dictionaries, but style guides prefer the short form. After an imperative the clause is a purpose, so the indicative "comprend" doesn't fit.

questions.stem: "Vous disez" for "vous dites" is …
questions.explanation: A form that doesn't exist in the language is a barbarism. A solecism puts existing words together wrongly; an abuse of language uses a real word too loosely.

questions.stem: "Le livre que je t'ai parlé" (for "dont je t'ai parlé") is …
questions.explanation: Every word exists, but the construction is wrong (parler de needs dont): a solecism.

questions.stem: What does Le Bon Usage do?
choices: It is the Académie française's dictionary.
It is a Québec government website.
It describes usage with many quotations from writers, and gives advice.
questions.explanation: Le Bon Usage, begun by Maurice Grevisse, is a grammar that records how French is really written, with quotations, then advises. The Académie publishes its own dictionary; the OQLF's Banque de dépannage linguistique is the Québec site.

questions.stem: For the writing paper of the DELF, what is the safe choice with a contested construction?
choices: Follow the norm, or use a noun instead.
Use the form you hear most often.
Write both forms with a slash.
questions.explanation: A marker may accept après qu'il soit parti, but nobody will penalise après qu'il est parti or après son départ. Avoiding the subjunctive isn't possible at B2.

questions.stem: What is a normative grammar?
choices: one that records usage without judging it
one that says what you should write
one that only lists spelling rules
questions.explanation: Normatif = prescriptive: it states the norm. A grammar that records usage without judging is descriptive.

questions.stem: Rewrite with a noun, as many style guides suggest: "Après qu'il est parti" → "Après son ___"
questions.explanation: Partir → le départ: après son départ avoids the après que question altogether.

questions.stem: Correct this for an exam with one word: "Malgré que la réunion ait commencé tard" → "___ que la réunion ait commencé tard"
questions.explanation: Bien que + subjunctive is the normative "although" (quoique, one word, also works, but it replaces the whole "malgré que"). The subjunctive ait commencé stays.

questions.stem: Match each contested form with the form the norm recommends.
left: de façon à ce qu'on comprenne
je me rappelle de ce jour
questions.explanation: Bien que for although; pallier with a direct object; après que with the indicative; de façon que for purpose; se rappeler with a direct object (or je me souviens de ce jour).

questions.stem: Which of these does the OQLF accept as standard? Select all that apply.
choices: Après qu'il soit arrivé, on a mangé.
Il faut pallier au manque de place.
questions.explanation: Se rappeler de is accepted before a personal pronoun and before an infinitive saying what not to forget. Après que + subjunctive and pallier à are criticised.

questions.stem: Put the steps in the order the lesson describes, from a new usage to the norm.
choices: Dictionaries record it, often with a label.
Schools and exams teach the norm.
questions.explanation: Usage comes first; descriptive works record it; normative authorities (the Académie, style guides) judge it; schools teach the result. A widespread usage can later be accepted.

questions.stem: When and where did the Lumière brothers hold their first paid public screening?
choices: on 28 December 1895, at the Grand Café in Paris
questions.explanation: 28 December 1895, in the Salon indien of the Grand Café, boulevard des Capucines. 1939 is the Cannes festival that never took place.

questions.stem: Which film did Georges Méliès make in 1902?
questions.explanation: Méliès's Voyage dans la Lune (1902) is famous for its tricks. À bout de souffle (Godard, 1960) and Les Quatre Cents Coups (Truffaut, 1959) are New Wave films; Le Dernier Été is the invented film of lesson 08.

questions.stem: When did the first Cannes festival actually take place?
questions.explanation: It was planned for September 1939 but the war stopped it; it opened in 1946. 1955 is the first Palme d'or; 1976 the first César awards.

questions.stem: What did François Truffaut win at Cannes in 1959 for Les Quatre Cents Coups?
questions.explanation: Truffaut received the prix de la mise en scène (best director) in 1959. The César didn't exist until 1976.

questions.stem: Why "Quelles" in "Quelles qu'aient été les craintes des artistes du muet"?
choices: It agrees with les craintes, feminine plural.
questions.explanation: In quel que soit (here in the subjonctif passé, quelles qu'aient été), quel agrees with the noun subject that follows: les craintes, feminine plural.

questions.stem: In standard written French, complete: "Bien que d'autres inventeurs ___ travaillé sur des machines voisines, c'est ce nom qui est resté."
questions.explanation: Bien que takes the subjunctive in standard French, and the work came before: subjonctif passé, qu'ils aient travaillé. "Ont" and "avaient" are indicative; "aies" is the tu form.

questions.stem: What does a chef opérateur (or cheffe opératrice) do?
choices: is in charge of the camera and the lighting
questions.explanation: Le chef opérateur is the director of photography. Directing is the réalisateur's or cinéaste's job, raising money the producteur's, and editing the monteur's.

questions.stem: "Le cinéma muet" is …
questions.explanation: Muet = silent: films without recorded speech, before sound arrived around 1929–1930 in France. Talking pictures are le cinéma parlant.

questions.stem: Who created the César awards, first presented in 1976?
questions.explanation: Georges Cravenne created the César, on the model of the Oscars; the first ceremony was held in Paris on 3 April 1976.

questions.stem: Write one word: "C'est un film ___ à Cannes."  (award-winning)
questions.explanation: Primé = award-winning: un film primé à Cannes (feminine primée).

questions.stem: Write the verb in the conditionnel: "Quand bien même ce film ___ primé, je ne l'aimerais pas."  (être)
questions.explanation: Quand bien même + conditionnel: quand bien même ce film serait primé.

questions.stem: Match each film or invention with the person behind it.
questions.explanation: Godard made À bout de souffle (1960), Truffaut Les Quatre Cents Coups (1959), Méliès Le Voyage dans la Lune (1902); the Lumière brothers built the cinématographe. Georges Cravenne created the César awards.

questions.stem: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
choices: The first Cannes festival was planned for 1939.
Méliès directed Les Quatre Cents Coups.
questions.explanation: Cannes was planned for September 1939 and first held in 1946; sound reached France around 1929–1930. The César began in 1976, and Les Quatre Cents Coups is Truffaut's.

questions.stem: Name the event at each numbered date on the timeline.

image.alt: A timeline from 1890 to 1980 with six numbered dots and date boxes: 1895, 1902, about 1929 to 1930, 1946, 1959 to 1960 and 1976.

questions.explanation: 1895 the Lumières' paid screening; 1902 Méliès's film; around 1929–1930 sound; 1946 the first Cannes festival; 1959–1960 the New Wave; 1976 the first César. Truffaut won the directing prize at Cannes, not the Palme d'or.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct in standard French?
choices: Pour peu qu'il fasse beau, la plage sera noire de monde.
Pour peu qu'il fait beau, la plage sera noire de monde.
Pour peu qu'il fera beau, la plage sera noire de monde.
Pour peu qu'il ferait beau, la plage sera noire de monde.
questions.explanation: Pour peu que takes the subjunctive: "qu'il fasse beau". The indicative "fait", the futur "fera" and the conditionnel "ferait" don't follow it. ("Noire de monde" = packed with people.)

questions.stem: Complete: "Nous partirons en juillet, sauf si les prix ___ trop élevés."
questions.explanation: Sauf si keeps the grammar of si: the indicative, and no futur or conditionnel straight after it, so "sauf si les prix sont trop élevés". The subjunctive "soient" belongs to à moins que ("à moins que les prix ne soient trop élevés"), which means the same.

questions.stem: Complete in careful written French: "Dans l'hypothèse où le seuil ___ dépassé, l'accès serait limité."
questions.explanation: Dans l'hypothèse où, like au cas où and dans le cas où, takes the conditionnel: "dans l'hypothèse où le seuil serait dépassé". In careful writing the futur "sera" doesn't follow it (some administrative texts use the indicative, but not careful prose), the subjunctive "soit" never does, and "a été" (it has been exceeded) clashes with a hypothesis about the future.

questions.stem: Which connector shows that the speaker doubts the condition will be met at all?
questions.explanation: "Si tant est que" = if indeed (and I doubt it): "Le sentier rouvrira en mai, si tant est que les travaux soient finis." "Pour peu que" says a small condition is enough, "à condition que" sets a requirement, and "en cas de" + noun plans for an event.

questions.stem: "En admettant que les quotas soient efficaces, ils déplacent le problème ailleurs." What does the writer do here?
choices: States as a fact that quotas work well.
Sets a condition for introducing quotas.
Grants a point for the sake of argument, then objects.
Says that quotas will be introduced elsewhere.
questions.explanation: "En admettant que" = even if we accept that: the writer grants that quotas may work, then raises an objection (they move the problem elsewhere). The subjunctive "soient" shows the point is granted, not stated as a fact.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: En cas de pluie, la visite est annulée.
En cas où il pleut, la visite est annulée.
En cas de pleuvoir, la visite est annulée.
Sauf si pluie, la visite est annulée.
questions.explanation: "En cas de" takes a noun with no article: "en cas de pluie". "En cas où" mixes it up with "au cas où" (which takes the conditionnel: "au cas où il pleuvrait"), "en cas de" isn't followed by an infinitive, and "sauf si" needs a clause ("sauf s'il pleut").

questions.stem: "Tu me l'aurais dit, je serais venu." What does this mean?
choices: You told me, so I came.
You would tell me, and I would come.
You must have told me that I'd come.
If you'd told me, I'd have come.
questions.explanation: Two conditionnels passés side by side (juxtaposition) work like a si-clause in speech: "Si tu me l'avais dit, je serais venu." Neither event happened. It's not a report of facts, a habit or a guess.

questions.stem: "Serait-il ministre, il ne changerait rien." What does this literary sentence mean?
choices: Is he a minister? He won't change anything.
Even if he were a minister, he wouldn't change anything.
He would be a minister if he changed nothing.
Since he is a minister, he changes nothing.
questions.explanation: A conditionnel with the subject after the verb, at the start of a sentence, means "even if" in literary French: "même s'il était ministre". It's not a question (no question mark) and not a statement of fact. Recognise it; you don't need to write it.

questions.stem: "À défaut de train, prenez le car." What does this mean?
choices: If there's no train, take the coach.
Instead of the coach, take the train.
Because the train is late, take the coach.
After the train, take the coach.
questions.explanation: "À défaut de" = failing, for want of (= faute de): if there's no train, take the coach. It doesn't express a preference, a cause or an order in time.

questions.stem: "En réservant tôt, vous paierez moins." Which si-sentence means the same?
choices: Si vous réserviez tôt, vous payiez moins.
Quand vous avez réservé tôt, vous avez payé moins.
Si vous réservez tôt, vous paierez moins.
Si vous réserverez tôt, vous paierez moins.
questions.explanation: The gérondif "en réservant" works as a condition about the future: si + present, then the futur. "Si vous réserviez …, vous payiez" describes a past habit, "Quand vous avez réservé" a past fact, and "si vous réserverez" breaks the rule: no futur after si.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si on ___, on aurait trouvé un hébergement."
questions.explanation: An unreal past condition: si + plus-que-parfait, then the conditionnel passé (on aurait trouvé): "Si on avait réservé". No conditionnel after si, so neither "aurait réservé" nor "réserverait"; "a réservé" would go with a futur or a present.

questions.stem:
Read the notice.

"Île de Lavin (commune inventée). À partir du 1er juin, l'accès à l'île sera limité à 1 500 visiteurs par jour en haute saison. Les habitants et les personnes qui ont réservé un hébergement sur l'île ne sont pas concernés. Les visiteurs à la journée devront acheter leur billet de navette en ligne, sauf s'ils ont moins de 12 ans. En cas de forte affluence, la navette pourra être suspendue sans préavis."

Who has to buy a shuttle ticket online?
choices: People staying overnight on the island
questions.explanation: "Les visiteurs à la journée devront acheter leur billet … sauf s'ils ont moins de 12 ans": day visitors, unless they are under 12. Residents and guests with accommodation on the island "ne sont pas concernés" by the limit. ("Sans préavis" = without notice.)

questions.stem: Complete: "En août, la plage est ___ : on ne trouve plus une place pour poser sa serviette."
questions.explanation: "Saturée" = overcrowded, full: there's no room left for a towel. "Préservée" (protected), "réglementée" (regulated) and "authentique" don't explain why there's no space.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio news item. Which statement is true?

audio.text: Flash info. Face à l'afflux de visiteurs, la mairie de Port-Lavin a décidé de réglementer l'accès au sentier côtier. À partir de juillet, la réservation sera obligatoire en haute saison, sauf pour les habitants de la commune. Elle restera gratuite. En cas de forte chaleur, le sentier pourra être fermé l'après-midi.

choices: Residents will have to book too.
The path will close every afternoon in July.
Booking will be required all year round.
questions.explanation: "La réservation sera obligatoire en haute saison, sauf pour les habitants … Elle restera gratuite." Residents are exempt, booking applies only in the high season, and the path may close in the afternoon only "en cas de forte chaleur".

questions.stem: Listen to Damien's voicemail. What condition comes with the cheap accommodation?

audio.text: Salut Chloé, c'est Damien. Pour le week-end en Bretagne, j'ai trouvé un hébergement pas cher, à condition qu'on arrive avant vingt heures. Sinon, il faudrait payer une nuit de plus. Je réserve, sauf si tu préfères partir samedi matin. Rappelle-moi avant ce soir !

choices: They must leave on Saturday morning.
They must pay for an extra night.
questions.explanation: "J'ai trouvé un hébergement pas cher, à condition qu'on arrive avant vingt heures. Sinon, il faudrait payer une nuit de plus." Paying an extra night is what happens if they arrive late; Saturday morning is Chloé's possible preference, and "avant ce soir" is when she should call back.

questions.stem: Complete with the two-word connector that means "unless" and takes the indicative: "Nous partirons en juillet, ___ les prix sont trop élevés."
questions.explanation: "Sauf si" + indicative: "sauf si les prix sont trop élevés". "À moins que" means the same but takes the subjunctive ("à moins que les prix ne soient …"), and "même si" (even if) changes the meaning.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "If the weather is even slightly good, the coves are overrun."
questions.explanation: "Pour peu qu'il fasse beau, les calanques sont prises d'assaut." The condition comes first, with pour peu que + subjunctive; "être pris d'assaut" = to be stormed, overrun.

questions.stem: Match each connector to what follows it.
questions.explanation: Pour peu que (like à supposer que, en admettant que, si tant est que) + subjunctive; dans l'hypothèse où, like au cas où, + conditionnel; sauf si and selon que + indicative; en cas de + a noun without an article (en cas d'urgence).

questions.stem: Which of these connectors take the subjunctive? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: À supposer que, si tant est que and en admettant que take the subjunctive. Sauf si and même si take the indicative (with the tenses of si), and dans l'hypothèse où takes the conditionnel.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this harbour town in high season.

image.alt: A harbour town in high season with five numbered markers: 1, a large cruise ship at the quay; 2, a dense crowd of people on the quay; 3, a hotel with a COMPLET sign; 4, a gate on a hill path under a sign reading Sur réservation, 400 personnes par jour; 5, a shop with the sign VOYAGES AZUR, circuits, croisières.

questions.explanation: 1 the cruise ship (le bateau de croisière); 2 the crowd pouring onto the quay (l'afflux de touristes); 3 the hotel marked COMPLET (l'hébergement, accommodation); 4 the booking gate limited to 400 people a day (le quota); 5 the travel shop selling tours and cruises (le voyagiste, tour operator). Nothing shows a low season or ecotourism.

questions.stem: "Le séisme aurait fait au moins vingt victimes." What does this news sentence mean?
choices: The earthquake reportedly killed at least twenty people.
The earthquake would have killed at least twenty people.
The earthquake will have killed at least twenty people.
The earthquake should have killed at least twenty people.
questions.explanation: In the news, the conditionnel passé gives unconfirmed information about a past event: "reportedly, is said to have". There is no si or sans here, so it isn't "would have"; "will have" would be the futur antérieur (aura fait).

questions.stem: Which sentence presents an unconfirmed fact?
choices: La préfecture a confirmé que deux randonneurs sont bloqués.
Si la route était coupée, deux randonneurs seraient bloqués.
Selon les secours, deux randonneurs seraient bloqués.
Deux randonneurs sont bloqués depuis hier.
questions.explanation: "Selon les secours, … seraient bloqués": a source and the conditionnel = reported, not confirmed. "Si la route était coupée …" uses the same verb form for a hypothesis, and the other two state confirmed facts in the indicative.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a hypothesis, not a news report?
choices: D'après la mairie, la crue aurait dévasté trois fermes.
Sans les digues, la crue aurait dévasté le village.
Le pont se serait effondré vers minuit, selon un témoin.
Selon la police, le feu serait parti d'un barbecue.
questions.explanation: "Sans les digues, la crue aurait dévasté le village" imagines what would have happened without the dykes: it didn't happen. The other three name a source (la mairie, un témoin, la police) and pass on something that reportedly did happen.

questions.stem: The journalist can't confirm this yet. Complete: "Les deux alpinistes ___ sains et saufs, selon les sauveteurs."
questions.explanation: Unconfirmed information about a present situation: conditionnel présent of être, plural for "les deux alpinistes": "seraient sains et saufs". "Serait" is singular, "sain et sauf" goes with être, not avoir, and the futur "seront" predicts instead of reporting.

questions.stem: Complete: "Selon un témoin, la voiture ___ emportée par la crue."
questions.explanation: A passive (être emporté) in the conditionnel passé: "aurait été emportée". Être takes avoir as its own auxiliary (j'ai été), so "serait été" is impossible, and "aurait eu" or "serait eue" use the wrong verb.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si nous avions un bateau, ___ les habitants nous-mêmes."
questions.explanation: Si + imparfait → conditionnel présent. Secourir has the stem secourr- (double r, like courir): "nous secourrions". "Nous secourions" (one r) is the imparfait, and "secouririons" and "secourerions" aren't forms of the verb.

questions.stem: "Tu aurais dû évacuer plus tôt !" Which use of the conditionnel is this?
questions.explanation: "Tu aurais dû" + infinitive = you should have: a reproach about something not done. There's no source (so it isn't reported news), it's not softening a request, and nothing is reported from the past.

questions.stem: "On dirait que tu serais le sauveteur et moi, je serais coincé sur le toit." Who would most likely say this?
choices: A child setting up a game
A judge summing up a case
questions.explanation: "On dirait que tu serais …" is the conditionnel of imaginary play: children use it to share out roles (let's pretend you're the rescuer). A news report would name a source, and an order would use the imperative.

questions.stem: "Moi, j'aurais menti ? Jamais !" What is the speaker doing?
questions.explanation: A question in the conditionnel that repeats what someone else claims expresses indignation: "Me, lie? Never!" The speaker denies it; "jamais" makes it clear.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le maire avait annoncé que l'école ___ le lundi suivant, mais elle est restée fermée."
questions.explanation: A future seen from a past moment (the announcement) takes the conditionnel présent: "il avait annoncé que l'école rouvrirait". The futur "rouvrira" doesn't fit a plan that has already failed ("elle est restée fermée"), and "rouvrirais" is the je / tu form.

questions.stem: Which word names a person who has lost their home or property in a disaster?
questions.explanation: "Le sinistré, la sinistrée" = disaster victim who has suffered damage. "Le sinistre" (B1) is the disaster itself or the insurance claim; "le sauveteur" is the rescuer; "le rescapé" is a survivor, someone who came out alive, not necessarily someone who lost property.

questions.stem: Complete: "Les sauveteurs fouillent ___ de l'immeuble effondré."
questions.explanation: "Les décombres" = rubble, what's left of a collapsed building; rescuers search it. A river in spate, an alert and bad weather aren't things you search through.

questions.stem:
Read the dispatch.

"Un feu de forêt s'est déclaré mardi en fin d'après-midi dans le massif de la Roche-Noire (lieu inventé). Selon les pompiers, il aurait été provoqué par une cigarette jetée d'une voiture. Trois cents hectares ont brûlé. Un camping aurait été évacué pendant la nuit, mais la préfecture ne l'a pas confirmé. Aucun blessé n'est à déplorer."

Which information does the journalist present as confirmed?
choices: A campsite was evacuated during the night.
The fire is now under control.
questions.explanation: "Trois cents hectares ont brûlé" is in the indicative, with no source: confirmed. The cigarette ("aurait été provoqué", selon les pompiers) and the campsite ("aurait été évacué", not confirmed) are reported in the conditionnel, and the dispatch doesn't say the fire is under control.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio news. Which information is confirmed?

audio.text: Il est sept heures. Un séisme a frappé cette nuit le sud de l'île de Sainte-Aurore. Selon les premiers bilans, il y aurait au moins douze blessés. Plusieurs bâtiments se seraient effondrés dans le centre-ville. Les autorités ont ouvert une cellule de crise et demandent aux habitants de ne pas rentrer chez eux.

choices: A crisis unit has been opened.
At least twelve people are injured.
The earthquake hit the north of the island.
questions.explanation: "Les autorités ont ouvert une cellule de crise": indicative, confirmed. The injuries ("il y aurait au moins douze blessés") and the buildings ("se seraient effondrés") are reported in the conditionnel, and the earthquake hit the south of the island, not the north.

questions.stem: Listen to the two speakers. According to the second speaker, what is certain?

audio.text: Tu as lu ? Le barrage aurait cédé cette nuit ! — Attends, c'est une rumeur. La mairie dit que le barrage tient, mais qu'on évacue les maisons près de la rivière par précaution.

choices: The dam gave way during the night.
The town hall has refused to evacuate anyone.
The river has already flooded the town.
Houses near the river are being evacuated as a precaution.
questions.explanation: The first speaker repeats a rumour in the conditionnel ("le barrage aurait cédé"). The second corrects it: the town hall says the dam is holding ("tient"), but "on évacue les maisons près de la rivière par précaution". Nothing is said about a flood in the town.

questions.stem: Rewrite as unconfirmed information. "L'ouragan a dévasté l'île." → "L'ouragan ___ l'île."
questions.explanation: Passé composé → conditionnel passé: only the auxiliary changes, "a" → "aurait": "L'ouragan aurait dévasté l'île" (the hurricane reportedly devastated the island).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "According to the emergency services, the driver is reportedly safe and sound."
questions.explanation: "Selon les secours, le conducteur serait sain et sauf." The source comes first, then the conditionnel présent "serait" for a present situation, and the fixed phrase "sain et sauf".

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the use of the conditionnel.
questions.explanation: Vous auriez … ? softens a request; tu aurais dû = you should have; se serait effondré passes on an unconfirmed report; viendrait is a future seen from the past (il a dit); j'aurais tant voulu expresses regret.

questions.stem: Which sentences present information as unconfirmed? Select all that apply.
choices: Selon la police, le suspect serait en fuite.
La préfecture a confirmé trois évacuations.
Le bilan serait provisoire, d'après les secours.
questions.explanation: Le suspect serait en fuite, l'incendie aurait détruit and le bilan serait provisoire are reportive conditionnels (two with a source). "La préfecture a confirmé" is a confirmed fact, and "Si j'étais toi, je partirais" is advice built on a hypothesis.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this flood scene.

image.alt: A flooded village with five numbered markers: 1, wide water with waves covering the lower part of the picture; 2, a collapsed house, a pile of bricks and a broken beam; 3, a person in a helmet and an orange vest in a small boat, holding a pole; 4, five people wrapped in blankets on dry ground next to a white tent marked Centre d'accueil; 5, a long tongue of brown mud running down a green hillside, with a fallen tree.

questions.explanation: 1 the river in spate covering the street (la crue); 2 the rubble of the collapsed house (les décombres); 3 the rescuer in the boat (le sauveteur); 4 the flood victims in blankets at the reception centre (les sinistrés); 5 the mud sliding down the hill (le glissement de terrain). There's no volcano and no tidal wave.

questions.stem: "Elle n'est pas venue à la réunion. Elle a dû se tromper de date." What does the second sentence mean?
choices: She must have got the date wrong.
She had to get the date wrong.
She should have got the date wrong.
She may get the date wrong.
questions.explanation: After a puzzling fact, "elle a dû" + infinitive is a guess about the past: she must have. "Had to" (obligation) makes no sense with a mistake, "should have" would be "elle aurait dû", and "may" would be "elle peut se tromper".

questions.stem: "Il devait être minuit quand la comète est apparue." What does this mean?
choices: It had to be midnight for the comet to appear.
It should be midnight when the comet appears.
It must have been about midnight when the comet appeared.
It was going to be midnight after the comet appeared.
questions.explanation: The imparfait of devoir in a past scene gives a guess about that moment: "it must have been midnight". It doesn't state a condition for the comet, and the sentence is in the past.

questions.stem: "La sonde devrait atteindre Jupiter en 2031." What does this mean?
choices: The probe should have reached Jupiter in 2031.
The probe is expected to reach Jupiter in 2031.
The probe must have reached Jupiter in 2031.
The probe had to reach Jupiter in 2031.
questions.explanation: The conditionnel présent of devoir gives an expectation about the future: "should, is expected to". "Should have" would be "aurait dû atteindre", "must have" "a dû atteindre", and 2031 is in the future.

questions.stem: How do you say "He may have forgotten the time"?
questions.explanation: "Il a pu" + infinitive (or "il peut avoir oublié") = he may have: a possibility. "Il a dû oublier" = he must have (more certain), "il aurait dû oublier" = he should have forgotten, and "il pourrait oublier" = he could forget (later).

questions.stem: Complete in standard French: "Il est peu probable que l'astéroïde ___ la Terre."
questions.explanation: "Il est peu probable que" leans towards "probably not", so it takes the subjunctive: "qu'il atteigne". The futur "atteindra", the present indicative "atteint" and the conditionnel "atteindrait" are indicative or conditionnel forms.

questions.stem: Complete in standard French: "Il y a fort à parier que la mission ___ prolongée."
questions.explanation: "Il y a fort à parier que" (it's a safe bet that) expresses high probability and takes the indicative: "la mission sera prolongée". "Soit" is a subjunctive, "sois" the je / tu form, and "fût" a literary imperfect subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which expression says the speaker is certain?
questions.explanation: "À coup sûr" = for certain. "Sans doute" is a trap: it means "probably" (certain is "sans aucun doute"); "peut-être" and "il se peut que" express possibility.

questions.stem: "Il viendra sans doute demain." What does this mean?
choices: He'll definitely come tomorrow, there's no doubt.
questions.explanation: "Sans doute" = probably, despite the English "without doubt". For certainty, French says "sans aucun doute" or "à coup sûr".

questions.stem: Complete: "___ décoller : il reste dix secondes."
choices: La fusée est sur le point de
questions.explanation: Ten seconds before launch, the rocket is about to take off: "est sur le point de décoller". "Vient de" = has just (after), "a fini par" = finally did, and "s'est mise à" = started (an activity).

questions.stem: "J'ai failli rater le lancement." What happened?
choices: I had just missed the launch.
I nearly missed the launch, but I saw it.
I ended up missing the launch.
questions.explanation: "Faillir" + infinitive = to nearly do something that didn't happen. So the speaker didn't miss it. "I missed it" would be "j'ai raté", "had just" "je venais de rater", "ended up" "j'ai fini par rater".

questions.stem: "L'astronaute ne va pas tarder à sortir de la capsule." What does this mean?
choices: The astronaut won't come out of the capsule.
The astronaut will come out of the capsule soon.
The astronaut is late coming out of the capsule.
The astronaut has just come out of the capsule.
questions.explanation: "Ne pas tarder à" + infinitive = not to be long before doing it: soon. The negative is part of the phrase; it doesn't mean the action won't happen.

questions.stem: Which word names the state of floating with no felt weight, as in a space station?
questions.explanation: "L'apesanteur" = weightlessness: "les astronautes vivent en apesanteur". "La gravité" is gravity (the pull itself), "l'orbite" the path around a body, and "l'exploration" the act of exploring.

questions.stem:
Read the news item.

"La sonde européenne Lyra (mission inventée) ne répond plus depuis lundi. Selon les ingénieurs, elle a dû passer dans l'ombre de l'astéroïde qu'elle étudie, ce qui couperait ses panneaux solaires du Soleil. Il se peut aussi qu'une antenne ait été endommagée. Il est en revanche exclu que la sonde se soit écrasée : sa trajectoire ne le permet pas. Le contact devrait être rétabli d'ici vendredi."

Which explanation do the engineers rule out?
choices: The probe passed into the asteroid's shadow.
The probe crashed onto the asteroid.
Contact will be restored by Friday.
questions.explanation: "Il est exclu que la sonde se soit écrasée": the crash is ruled out. The shadow is their most likely explanation ("elle a dû"), the antenna a possibility ("il se peut que"), and contact by Friday an expectation ("devrait").

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. From where will the comet be hard to see?

audio.text: Bonne nouvelle pour les amateurs d'astronomie : la comète Hélios devrait être visible à l'œil nu à partir du 12 mars. Les astronomes estiment qu'elle sera la plus brillante vers le 20. Il est peu probable, en revanche, qu'on puisse la voir depuis les grandes villes, à cause de la pollution lumineuse.

questions.explanation: "Il est peu probable, en revanche, qu'on puisse la voir depuis les grandes villes, à cause de la pollution lumineuse" (light pollution). The mountains, the sea and the south aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: Listen to the two speakers. What does the second speaker think?

audio.text: Les extraterrestres existent, c'est sûr. Avec des milliards de planètes ! — Qu'il y ait de la vie ailleurs, d'accord, c'est même probable. Mais qu'elle nous rende visite, il est exclu que ça arrive de notre vivant.

choices: Aliens have already visited the Earth.
Life can exist only on planets like the Earth.
Life elsewhere is likely, but an alien visit in our lifetime is ruled out.
questions.explanation: The second speaker accepts that life elsewhere is probable ("c'est même probable") but says "il est exclu que ça arrive de notre vivant" about a visit. The first speaker is the one who is sure aliens exist.

questions.stem: Translate with devoir: "She must have forgotten." → "Elle ___ oublier."
questions.explanation: Probability about the past: devoir in the passé composé + infinitive: "Elle a dû oublier." (The same idea with the past on the infinitive: "Elle doit avoir oublié.") Write the circumflex on dû.

questions.stem: Put these phrases in order, from before an action starts to just after it ends.
questions.explanation: Before: être sur le point de (about to); start: se mettre à; during: être en train de; end: finir par; just after: venir de.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Doit être = probably is; a pu se perdre = may have got lost; il est exclu que + subjunctive = it's out of the question; a failli = nearly (and didn't); vient de = has just. "He had to leave" would be "il a dû partir" in its obligation sense.

questions.stem: Which expressions are followed by the subjunctive in standard French? Select all that apply.
choices: il y a fort à parier que
questions.explanation: Possibility, unlikelihood and exclusion take the subjunctive: il se peut que, il est peu probable que, il est exclu que. High probability and certainty take the indicative: il y a fort à parier que, il est fort probable que, je suis certain que.

questions.stem: Name the numbered objects in this corner of the solar system.

image.alt: A corner of the solar system with the Sun and the Earth labelled, and five numbered markers: 1, on a dashed ellipse around the Sun; 2, on a box-shaped spacecraft with two solar panels and a dish; 3, on a white ball with a long pale tail; 4, on a lumpy rock with two craters; 5, on a small structure near the Earth made of a module, a beam and four solar panels.
