questions.explanation: 1 the path around the Sun (l'orbite); 2 the spacecraft heading for the comet (la sonde); 3 the ball with a tail (la comète); 4 the cratered rock (l'astéroïde); 5 the structure orbiting the Earth (la station spatiale). There's no black hole or galaxy in the picture.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Plus les prix montent, moins on épargne.
Le plus les prix montent, le moins on épargne.
Plus que les prix montent, moins que on épargne.
Plus les prix montent, le moins on épargne.
questions.explanation: Proportion: plus / moins at the head of each clause, with no article and no que: "Plus les prix montent, moins on épargne." "Le plus … le moins" copies English "the more … the less".

questions.stem: "Autant il est économe, autant sa sœur est dépensière." What does this mean?
choices: The more he saves, the more his sister spends.
He is as extravagant as his sister.
He is thrifty, whereas his sister is extravagant.
He and his sister are both thrifty.
questions.explanation: "Autant … autant" sets two things side by side in contrast: he's as thrifty as she is extravagant. It isn't a proportion (that would be "plus il épargne, plus sa sœur dépense").

questions.stem: Complete: "Les ménages épargnent, ___ l'avenir est incertain."
questions.explanation: "D'autant plus que" + indicative = all the more so because: the uncertain future strengthens the reason to save. "À mesure que" needs two changes moving together, "plutôt que" (rather than) and "comme si" (as if) don't fit the meaning.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il faut réduire nos dépenses, d'autant plus que les prix ___ encore."
questions.explanation: "D'autant plus que" introduces a real cause and takes the indicative: "les prix ont augmenté". The subjunctive "aient augmenté", the participle "ayant augmenté" and the infinitive can't follow it.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct in standard French?
choices: Elle est davantage riche que moi.
questions.explanation: "Davantage" = plus after a verb (épargner davantage) or before de + noun. Before an adjective or adverb, use plus: plus cher, plus riche, mieux.

questions.stem: Branded pasta costs 2 € a packet; the own brand costs 1 €. Which sentence is true?
choices: La marque de distributeur est deux fois moins chère.
La marque de distributeur est deux fois plus chère.
Les pâtes de marque sont deux fois moins chères.
Les deux produits coûtent le même prix.
questions.explanation: 1 € is half of 2 €: the own brand is "deux fois moins chère" (French says "two times less" for half the price), and the branded pasta is "deux fois plus chère".

questions.stem: Complete: "Il dépense comme s'il ___ au loto."
questions.explanation: "Comme si" works like si: the imparfait or the plus-que-parfait, never the conditionnel or the futur. "Comme s'il avait gagné au loto" = as if he had won the lottery.

questions.stem: Complete: "J'ai revendu la voiture ___ : je n'ai rien réparé."
questions.explanation: "Tel quel" = as it is, and both words agree with the noun: la voiture → "telle quelle". "Tel que" means "such as" and needs something after it.

questions.stem: Complete: "Notez vos dépenses ___ : ce sera plus facile à la fin du mois."
questions.explanation: "Au fur et à mesure" alone = as you go, bit by bit. "À mesure que", "d'autant plus que" and "plutôt que de" need a verb after them.

questions.stem: Someone who spends a lot and never puts money aside is…
questions.explanation: "Dépensier, dépensière" = extravagant, spending a lot. "Économe" is the opposite (thrifty); "abordable" (affordable) and "onéreux" (costly) describe prices, not people.

questions.stem: Which expression means "to make ends meet"?
questions.explanation: "Joindre les deux bouts" = to make ends meet. "Se serrer la ceinture" = to tighten your belt, "le rapport qualité-prix" = value for money, "la flambée des prix" = a surge in prices.

questions.stem:
Read the text.

"Selon l'Insee, la hausse des prix à la consommation est passée de 4,9 % en 2023 à 2,0 % en 2024, puis à 0,9 % en 2025. Les prix augmentent donc de moins en moins vite. Pour autant, ils ne reviennent pas à leur niveau d'avant 2022 : la flambée des prix reste visible dans les tickets de caisse."

What does the text say about prices in 2025?
choices: They returned to their level before 2022.
They still rose, but more slowly than in 2024.
questions.explanation: Inflation of 0.9 % means prices still rose, by less than in 2024 (2.0 %): "les prix augmentent de moins en moins vite". A fall would be a negative figure, and the text says prices don't go back to their pre-2022 level.

questions.stem: Listen to the consumer item. What advice does the speaker give?

audio.text: Dans les supermarchés, les marques de distributeur gagnent du terrain. Elles sont souvent nettement moins chères que les grandes marques. Plus les prix montent, plus les consommateurs se tournent vers elles. Mais attention : moins cher ne veut pas toujours dire meilleur rapport qualité-prix. Comparez les étiquettes.

questions.explanation: "Moins cher ne veut pas toujours dire meilleur rapport qualité-prix. Comparez les étiquettes." The speaker says own brands are popular and often cheaper, but doesn't tell you to always buy them.

questions.stem: Listen to the two speakers. What does the second speaker think?

audio.text: Avec l'inflation, on devrait arrêter d'épargner et profiter de la vie. — Au contraire ! Plus l'avenir est incertain, plus il faut mettre de l'argent de côté.

choices: The more uncertain the future, the more you should save.
You should stop saving and enjoy life.
Only the rich can save money.
questions.explanation: "Au contraire ! Plus l'avenir est incertain, plus il faut mettre de l'argent de côté." The second speaker rejects the first speaker's idea of stopping saving.

questions.stem: Complete with the one-word synonym of "plus" that goes after a verb: "Pour partir en vacances, il faudrait épargner ___."
questions.explanation: "Davantage" = plus, after a verb: "épargner davantage" (to save more). "Plus" would also be correct French, but the question asks for its synonym.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "The higher prices go, the less households save."
questions.explanation: "Plus les prix montent, moins les ménages épargnent." Each clause opens with plus or moins, with no article and no que.

questions.stem: Match each connector to its meaning.
questions.explanation: À mesure que = as, progressively; d'autant plus que = all the more so because; autant … autant contrasts two things; plutôt que de + infinitive = rather than; comme si + imparfait / plus-que-parfait = as if. "The more … the more" is plus … plus.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in standard French? Select all that apply.
choices: Plus on attend, plus c'est cher.
Plus on attend, et plus c'est cher.
Le plus on attend, le plus c'est cher.
questions.explanation: Proportion without or with et is correct ("Plus on attend, (et) plus c'est cher"); "le plus … le plus" copies English. "Travailler davantage" is correct; before an adjective, use plus: "c'est plus cher".

questions.stem: Name each numbered spending category in the Martin family's budget.

image.alt: A bar chart titled Le budget mensuel de la famille Martin (chiffres inventés), household income 2,200 euros a month, with five numbered icons and bars: 1, a house, 900 euros; 2, a shopping trolley, 550 euros; 3, a car, 300 euros; 4, a ticket, 200 euros; 5, a piggy bank, 250 euros.

questions.explanation: 1 the house = housing (le logement, 900 €); 2 the trolley = food (l'alimentation); 3 the car = transport (les transports); 4 the ticket = leisure (les loisirs); 5 the piggy bank = savings (l'épargne). Over-indebtedness and purchasing power aren't spending categories.

questions.stem: Complete in careful French: "Un Français sur cinq ___ en vacances moins d'une semaine."
questions.explanation: After "un … sur cinq", the subject is "un", so the verb is singular: "un Français sur cinq part".

questions.stem: Complete: "La plupart des ménages ___ une voiture."
questions.explanation: After "la plupart des" + plural noun, the verb is plural: "la plupart des ménages ont".

questions.stem: A rate goes from 8 % to 10 %. Which description is right?
choices: It has risen by 2 points, that is by 25 %.
It has risen by 2 points, that is by 20 %.
questions.explanation: 10 − 8 = 2 percentage points. In relative terms, 2 is a quarter of 8, so the rate rose by 25 %. "2 %" confuses points and percent; 20 % would be right only from a starting point of 10 %.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le chômage est passé ___ 7,5 % ___ 7,1 %."
questions.explanation: "Passer de … à …" = to go from … to …: "de 7,5 % à 7,1 %".

questions.stem: Sales fell BY 30 %. Complete: "Les ventes ont chuté ___ 30 %."
questions.explanation: "De" + amount gives the size of the change (by): "chuter de 30 %". "Chuter à 30 %" would give the level reached (to 30 %), which isn't what the stem says.

questions.stem: Five monthly salaries: 1 900 €, 2 000 €, 2 100 €, 2 200 € and 11 800 €. What is the median?
questions.explanation: Put in order, the middle (third) value is 2 100 €: that's the median (la médiane). 4 000 € is the mean (20 000 ÷ 5), pulled up by the one high salary.

questions.stem: "Depuis deux ans, les salaires stagnent." What does this mean?
choices: Wages have fallen sharply for two years.
Wages have soared for two years.
Wages haven't been paid for two years.
Wages have hardly changed for two years.
questions.explanation: "Stagner" = to stand still, to be flat. A sharp fall would be "chuter", a strong rise "bondir" or "s'envoler".

questions.stem: Look at the graph. Which sentence describes it correctly?

image.alt: A line graph of the savings rate of households in Valmont (invented figures), 2018 to 2025: 14.0 in 2018, 14.6 in 2019, a peak of 21.0 in 2020, 18.2 in 2021, 16.1 in 2022, then 16.9, 17.0 and 17.1 from 2023 to 2025.

choices: Le taux n'a cessé d'augmenter depuis 2018.
Le taux a atteint un pic en 2020, puis il a baissé avant de se stabiliser autour de 17 %.
Le taux est plus bas en 2025 qu'en 2018.
questions.explanation: The curve jumps to a peak of 21 % in 2020, falls to 16.1 % in 2022 and then stays at about 17 %. It doesn't rise every year, it doesn't fall in 2020, and 17.1 % in 2025 is higher than 14.0 % in 2018.

questions.stem: A poll gives candidate A 51 % and candidate B 49 %, with a margin of error of about 3 points. What can you conclude?
choices: The poll can't say who is ahead.
questions.explanation: The gap (2 points) is smaller than the margin of error (about 3 points): "l'écart est inférieur à la marge d'erreur". The poll is consistent with either candidate leading.

questions.stem: "La majorité des sondés pense / pensent que …" Which statement is right?
choices: Both the singular and the plural are accepted.
Neither: you must say "la plupart des sondés".
questions.explanation: After a collective noun + des + plural (la majorité des, un tiers des), French grammars accept the verb in the singular (you see the group) or the plural (you see the people). Pick one and keep to it.

questions.stem: Type the French for "a third": "___ des ménages n'a pas de voiture."
questions.explanation: "Un tiers" = a third (the fraction): "Un tiers des ménages n'a pas de voiture" (the plural "n'ont pas" is also accepted after it). "Troisième" is the ordinal, the third one.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "The rate rose by two points."
questions.explanation: "Le taux a augmenté de deux points." De + amount gives the size of the change.

questions.stem: Match each verb to its meaning.
questions.explanation: From strong rise to strong fall: bondir (jump), progresser (rise), stagner (stay flat), reculer (fall back), chuter (plummet). "To double" is doubler.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Un tiers des ménages a une voiture.
Un tiers des ménages ont une voiture.
La plupart des ménages a une voiture.
Un Français sur cinq part en vacances.
Les prix ont augmenté à 3 % en un an.
questions.explanation: After "un tiers des", singular and plural are both accepted; after "la plupart des", the plural ("ont"); after "un … sur cinq", the singular. A rise of 3 % takes de: "ont augmenté de 3 %".

questions.stem: Where was Jules Verne born, and where did he die?
choices: Born in Nantes, died in Amiens
Born in Amiens, died in Nantes
Born in Paris, died in Nantes
Born in Nantes, died in Paris
questions.explanation: Verne was born in Nantes on 8 February 1828 and died in Amiens, where he had lived since the early 1870s, on 24 March 1905.

questions.stem: How did "De la Terre à la Lune" first reach readers in 1865?
choices: As a play in a Paris theatre
As an illustrated book for children only
As a serial in the Journal des débats
As a lecture at an observatory
questions.explanation: It first ran as a serial (en feuilleton) in the Journal des débats, from 14 September to 14 October 1865, then came out as a book from Hetzel.

questions.stem: In Verne's two Moon novels, what happens to the projectile?
choices: It lands on the Moon and stays there.
It circles the Moon and falls back into the Pacific.
It comes back down in Florida.
questions.explanation: Knocked off course by a small celestial body, the shell circles the Moon; a late attempt to correct its path with rockets fails, and it falls back into the Pacific, where a navy ship fishes the travellers out.

questions.stem: Which feature does Verne's story share with Apollo 8 (December 1968)?
choices: The crew is fired from a giant cannon.
The crew lands on the Moon.
The launch takes place in Baltimore.
Three men circle the Moon without landing and come down in the Pacific.
questions.explanation: Apollo 8 carried three astronauts, circled the Moon ten times without landing and splashed down in the Pacific. Verne's cannon has no Apollo equivalent, Apollo 8 didn't land, and Baltimore is only where Verne's Gun Club meets.

questions.stem: What did Verne get wrong about weightlessness?
choices: He said the travellers would feel heavier in space.
He left gravity out of the story.
He showed it only near the point where the Earth's and the Moon's pulls balance.
He said weightlessness lasted the whole trip.
questions.explanation: In the novel, the travellers float only near the balance point. In reality a coasting spacecraft is in free fall the whole way, so the crew float from the moment the engines stop: the whole trip.

questions.stem: Complete in standard French: "Il est peu probable que Verne ___ que les passagers seraient écrasés."
questions.explanation: "Il est peu probable que" takes the subjunctive, and the knowing comes before the main verb, so the subjonctif passé: "qu'il ait su". "A su", "avait su" and "saura" are indicative.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il y a fort à parier qu'en 1865, beaucoup de lecteurs ___ le voyage possible."
questions.explanation: "Il y a fort à parier que" takes the indicative, and "en 1865" puts the belief in the past: "ont cru". "Aient cru" is a subjunctive, and the present or future don't fit 1865.

questions.stem: Which word best describes a story that is hard to believe?
questions.explanation: "Invraisemblable" = implausible, far-fetched. "Prophétique" and "visionnaire" praise a work that foresaw the future; "abordable" means affordable.

questions.stem: Complete: "À supposer que le canon ___ tirer l'obus, les voyageurs n'auraient pas survécu."
questions.explanation: "À supposer que" takes the subjunctive; the shot would come before the travellers' death, so the subjonctif passé "ait pu". "A pu" is indicative, "aurait pu" conditionnel, "pourra" futur.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le module d'Apollo 11 ___ le 20 juillet 1969."
questions.explanation: "Alunir" is conjugated like finir and takes avoir: "il a aluni" (participle aluni). It is formed like atterrir and amerrir.

questions.stem: Complete with the word for a story published in instalments in a newspaper: "Le roman a d'abord paru en ___ dans le Journal des débats."
questions.explanation: "Paraître en feuilleton" = to come out as a serial. Both Moon novels appeared this way before becoming books.

questions.stem: Put the events of the two novels in order.
choices: Le Gun Club cherche un nouveau défi.
On coule un canon géant en Floride.
Michel Ardan demande à voyager dans l'obus.
L'obus tourne autour de la Lune.
Un navire repêche les voyageurs dans le Pacifique.
questions.explanation: The bored Gun Club looks for a challenge; the cannon is cast in Florida; Ardan's telegram says he wants to travel inside an elongated projectile; the shell circles the Moon; a navy ship fishes the travellers out of the Pacific.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Le feuilleton = serial; invraisemblable = implausible; visionnaire = visionary; alunir = to land on the Moon; le projectile = projectile. "To take off" is décoller.

questions.stem: Which statements about Verne's Moon novels are true? Select all that apply.
choices: The launch takes place in Florida.
The travellers land on the Moon.
One of the travellers is French.
The sequel came out as a book in 1870.
The novels were first published in English.
questions.explanation: The cannon is in Florida, Michel Ardan is French, and Autour de la Lune came out as a book in January 1870 after its 1869 serial. The travellers never land, and the novels were written and first published in French.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le piratage a touché trois cents comptes, ___ celui du ministre."
questions.explanation: Dont introduces one part of a group just mentioned: trois cents comptes, dont celui du ministre (including the minister's). Que needs a verb whose object it is, où is for place or time, and lequel needs a preposition before it.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct in standard French?
choices: Elle a des abonnés partout, dont la plupart ne parlent pas français.
Elle a des abonnés partout, dont la plupart ne parle pas français.
Elle a des abonnés partout, que la plupart ne parlent pas français.
Elle a des abonnés partout, dont la plupart d'eux ne parlent pas français.
questions.explanation: Dont + la plupart picks out most of the followers, and la plupart takes a plural verb: dont la plupart ne parlent pas français. Que can't introduce a part of a group, and "la plupart d'eux" isn't French (la plupart d'entre eux, but not after dont, which already means "of them").

questions.stem: Complete in careful written French: "C'est un principe sur ___ repose tout le site."
questions.explanation: After a preposition and a noun antecedent (un principe), careful French uses lequel: sur lequel. Sur quoi is for ce, rien, quelque chose or voilà; after a noun it is literary. Sur qui is for people, and dont can't follow a preposition.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ce ___ je compte, c'est ta discrétion."
questions.explanation: Compter sur + ce: after ce, a preposition is followed by quoi, so ce sur quoi (what I'm counting on). Ce sur lequel isn't used, dont is for verbs with de, and que would make discrétion the direct object of compter, which takes sur.

questions.stem: What does "Il y a de quoi s'inquiéter" mean?
choices: What is there to worry about?
questions.explanation: De quoi + infinitive means "enough to, reason to": il y a de quoi s'inquiéter = there's good reason to worry. "Nothing to worry about" would be il n'y a pas de quoi s'inquiéter.

questions.stem: Which word gives the formal version of "sinon" here? "Payez avant vendredi, ___ votre compte sera suspendu."
questions.explanation: Sans quoi = or else, otherwise (formal): pay before Friday, or else your account will be suspended. Après quoi means "after which", which would make no sense here; de quoi and à quoi don't link two sentences.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je me souviens du jour ___ j'ai créé mon premier compte."
questions.explanation: After a noun of time (le jour, l'époque, le moment), French uses où: le jour où. Quand can't follow a noun like this, lequel needs a preposition, and dont is for de + noun.

questions.stem: How do you say "He has no one to confide in"?
choices: Il n'a personne à se confier.
Il n'a personne qui se confier.
Il n'a personne à qui se confier.
Il n'a personne dont se confier.
questions.explanation: Se confier à quelqu'un → a relative infinitive with the preposition kept: personne à qui se confier. English drops "in" at the end; French needs à qui before the infinitive. Qui alone and dont don't fit se confier à.

questions.stem: What does this sentence say? "Les utilisateurs, qui ont plus de 15 ans, peuvent ouvrir un compte."
choices: Only the users who are over 15 can open an account.
Users have to wait until they are 15 to use the site.
All the users are over 15, and they can open an account.
Some users over 15 can't open an account.
questions.explanation: The commas make the clause non-defining: it adds information about all the users (they are all over 15). Without commas, "Les utilisateurs qui ont plus de 15 ans peuvent ouvrir un compte" would mean only those over 15.

questions.stem: Which sentence says that only some internet users are exposed to hacking?
choices: Les internautes qui partagent leurs données sont exposés au piratage.
Les internautes, qui partagent leurs données, sont exposés au piratage.
Les internautes, lesquels partagent leurs données, sont exposés au piratage.
Les internautes partagent leurs données, et ils sont exposés au piratage.
questions.explanation: A defining relative clause, with no commas, picks out a subgroup: only those who share their data. The versions with commas (qui or the formal lequel) and the version with "et" describe all internet users.

questions.stem: In "J'ai écrit à la sœur de mon voisin, laquelle travaille dans la cybersécurité", who works in cybersecurity?
questions.explanation: Laquelle is feminine, so it refers to la sœur, not to mon voisin (masculine). Formal writing uses lequel / laquelle as a subject exactly to remove this kind of doubt; with qui, the sentence could be read either way.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ce n'est pas mon ordinateur, c'est ___ ma sœur se sert."
questions.explanation: Se servir de → dont, and the antecedent is a particular computer, so celui: celui dont ma sœur se sert (the one my sister uses). Celle dont is feminine, but ordinateur is masculine; que and qui don't fit a verb with de.

questions.stem: Complete in standard French: "C'est l'influenceur sur le compte ___ j'ai vu la vidéo."
questions.explanation: The antecedent follows a preposition + noun (sur le compte de l'influenceur), and dont can't complement a noun that comes after a preposition. Use duquel (or de qui for a person). Lequel would leave out the de.

questions.stem: What is "le droit à l'oubli"?
choices: the right to forget your password without paying a fee
a law that punishes online harassment
the right to use a site without giving your name
the right to have certain information about you removed or delisted
questions.explanation: Le droit à l'oubli is the right to be forgotten: asking a search engine to stop showing certain links about you, or having data erased. The right to stay anonymous is l'anonymat, and harassment is le harcèlement.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. How many teenagers say they have been cyberbullied?

audio.text: Selon une étude publiée ce matin, un adolescent sur cinq dit avoir déjà été victime de cyberharcèlement, dont la moitié plusieurs fois par mois.

choices: half of all teenagers, several times a month
questions.explanation: Un adolescent sur cinq = one teenager in five. Dont la moitié plusieurs fois par mois means "half of them several times a month": dont picks out a part of the group already counted, not half of all teenagers.

questions.stem: Listen to the voicemail. What will happen if you don't change your password before noon?

audio.text: Bonjour, ici le service client. Votre compte a été piraté cette nuit. Changez votre mot de passe avant midi, sans quoi nous devrons le bloquer. Après quoi, vous recevrez un nouveau code par SMS.

choices: You will receive a new code by text message.
questions.explanation: Sans quoi nous devrons le bloquer = or else we will have to block it. The code comes après quoi, after you have changed the password.

questions.stem: Complete with a preposition and a relative pronoun: "C'est quelque chose ___ je n'avais pas pensé."
questions.explanation: Penser à + quelque chose → à quoi: c'est quelque chose à quoi je n'avais pas pensé (something I hadn't thought of). After quelque chose, ce, rien and voilà, the pronoun after a preposition is quoi (with quelque chose, auquel is also accepted).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I have no one to talk to."
questions.explanation: Je n'ai personne à qui parler. The relative infinitive keeps the preposition of parler à before the pronoun: à qui parler.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to the word that fills the gap.
questions.explanation: Time after a noun → où. A part of a group → dont. Preposition after ce → quoi. Preposition after a noun (le site) → lequel.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in careful written French? Select all that apply.
choices: Voilà de quoi parler pendant des heures.
Il n'y a rien à quoi l'on puisse se fier.
L'utilisateur dont son compte a été piraté a porté plainte.
Il m'a montré l'application dont il se sert.
C'est le jour quand j'ai supprimé mon compte.
questions.explanation: De quoi + infinitive, rien à quoi and dont with se servir de are all correct. "Dont son compte" says "whose" twice: l'utilisateur dont le compte a été piraté. After le jour, use où, not quand.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this social-media screen.

image.alt: A phone screen showing a social network, with five numbered parts: a round profile picture at the top, a follower counter next to it, a bracket beside the column of posts, a post with a photo of a cat, and a padlock icon at the bottom.

questions.explanation: 1 is the profile of the person with many followers: l'influenceuse (masculine l'influenceur). 2 counts the followers: les abonnés. 3 marks the whole column of posts: le fil d'actualité. 4 is one post: la publication. 5, the padlock, leads to the privacy settings: la confidentialité.

questions.stem: Which noun group is correct?
questions.explanation: Nouns in -age, -ment and -isme are usually masculine: le tirage, le lancement, le pluralisme. Nouns in -ure are usually feminine: la censure.

questions.stem: What is the noun made from "refuser"?
questions.explanation: Refuser gives a bare-stem noun: le refus (like l'achat, la baisse). The other forms follow real suffixes but don't exist: always check the dictionary.

questions.stem: Turn the clause into a noun group: "Après que le rédacteur en chef est parti, …"
choices: Après la partie du rédacteur en chef, …
Après le partement du rédacteur en chef, …
Après le départ du rédacteur en chef, …
questions.explanation: The noun from partir is le départ, and the subject follows with de: le départ du rédacteur en chef. La partie means a part or a game; "partement" doesn't exist; an infinitive can't take son.

questions.stem: Complete: "En raison de ___ des prix, le journal coûte plus cher."
questions.explanation: La hausse (from hausser) is the usual noun for a rise in prices; l'augmentation would work too. Le haussement is used for shrugging (un haussement d'épaules), l'augmenté is a participle, and la haute is an adjective.

questions.stem: Complete: "La lutte ___ la désinformation est une priorité."
questions.explanation: Lutter contre → la lutte contre: the noun keeps the verb's preposition. "La lutte de la désinformation" would make disinformation the one fighting.

questions.stem: Complete: "Chaque citoyen a droit à l'accès ___ l'information."
questions.explanation: Accéder à → l'accès à. Learn the preposition with the noun: l'accès à, la participation à, l'intérêt pour, la lutte contre.

questions.stem: What does the headline "Démission surprise du rédacteur en chef" report?
choices: The editor-in-chief has surprised everyone by staying.
Readers are asking the editor-in-chief to resign.
The editor-in-chief has dismissed a journalist.
questions.explanation: Démission = resignation, and the noun after it (du rédacteur en chef) is the one resigning; surprise = unexpected. Put the verb back: Le rédacteur en chef démissionne, à la surprise générale.

questions.stem: Which headline is a nominal sentence?
choices: Le prix de l'électricité a encore augmenté
Hausse record du prix de l'électricité
questions.explanation: "Hausse record du prix de l'électricité" has no conjugated verb: it is built on the noun hausse. The other headlines have verbs: a augmenté, coûte, coûtera.

questions.stem: Rewrite in the nominal style, keeping the meaning: "Bien que les ventes aient baissé, le mensuel continue."
choices: En raison de la baisse des ventes, le mensuel continue.
Grâce à la baisse des ventes, le mensuel continue.
Malgré la baisse des ventes, le mensuel continue.
Avant la baisse des ventes, le mensuel continue.
questions.explanation: Bien que (concession) → malgré + noun: malgré la baisse des ventes. En raison de gives a cause, grâce à a good cause, and avant a time: all change the meaning.

questions.stem: What is "la manchette" of a newspaper?
choices: the banner headline across the front page
a news item of a few lines
questions.explanation: La manchette is the big headline across the top of the front page. A short item is la brève, the opinion piece l'éditorial, and the print run le tirage.

questions.stem: "Le tirage de ce quotidien a baissé." What has gone down?
choices: the number of copies printed or sold
questions.explanation: Le tirage is a paper's print run or circulation. (Le tirage au sort is a draw.)

questions.stem: Why can "la critique du ministre" be unclear?
choices: Critique is masculine here, so the article is wrong.
It can mean criticism by the minister or criticism of the minister.
It can only mean that the minister wrote a review.
questions.explanation: When a verb becomes a noun, both its subject and its object follow with de, so la critique du ministre can be the minister's criticism or criticism of the minister. Context, or a preposition such as contre, decides.

questions.stem: Which word names a journalist who works freelance and is paid by the piece?
questions.explanation: Le pigiste (la pigiste) is paid à la pige, by the piece. L'éditorialiste writes editorials, le rédacteur en chef runs the editorial staff, and le lectorat is the readership.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio headlines. What is said about the newsstands?

audio.text: Les titres de ce matin. Fermeture de trois kiosques à Lille : les marchands de journaux inquiets. Et dans la presse écrite, nouvelle baisse du lectorat des quotidiens.

choices: Three new newsstands are opening in Lille.
The sellers are protesting against a new law.
Three newsstands have sold out of newspapers.
Three are closing, and the sellers are worried.
questions.explanation: Fermeture de trois kiosques à Lille : les marchands de journaux inquiets = three newsstands are closing in Lille, and the newsagents are worried. The headline is a nominal sentence: put the verb back to understand it.

questions.stem: Listen. Why isn't the second speaker surprised by the editorial?

audio.text: Tu as lu l'éditorial ce matin ? Oui, mais rien de nouveau : c'est la ligne éditoriale habituelle, toujours contre le gouvernement. Moi, je préfère les hebdomadaires. Il y a plus de pluralisme.

choices: It follows the paper's usual editorial line.
It was written by a freelance journalist.
It was censored by the government.
questions.explanation: C'est la ligne éditoriale habituelle = it's the usual editorial line, always against the government. The conversation then turns to weeklies, which offer more pluralism.

questions.stem: Type the noun (without an article) that completes this headline, from the verb "fermer": "___ de l'usine : les salariés inquiets"
questions.explanation: Fermer → la fermeture (-ure, feminine). Headlines usually drop the article: Fermeture de l'usine : les salariés inquiets.

questions.stem: Match each verb to its noun.
questions.explanation: Publier → la publication (-tion), lancer → le lancement (-ment), tirer → le tirage (-age), censurer → la censure (-ure). "Le publiement" doesn't exist, and la lanceuse is a person (a woman who throws).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "After the publication of the investigation, the minister resigned."
questions.explanation: Après la publication de l'enquête, le ministre a démissionné. The noun group (après + la publication de …) replaces a clause (après que l'enquête a été publiée).

questions.stem: Which of these nouns are feminine? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Nouns in -ure and -ité are usually feminine: la fermeture, la censure, la liberté. Nouns in -age, -ment and -isme are usually masculine: le tirage, le lancement, le pluralisme.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this front page.

image.alt: The front page of an invented daily, Le Courrier du Matin, with four numbered parts: a large headline across the top, three grey lines under it, a short item in the left column, and a shaded box with a signature on the right.

questions.explanation: 1 is the banner headline: la manchette. 2 is the short paragraph that sums up the article: le chapeau (standfirst). 3 is a news item of a few lines: la brève. 4 is the signed opinion piece: l'éditorial. Le kiosque is where the paper is sold, and le lectorat its readers.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a correct formal alternative to "On a refusé l'entrée au journaliste"?
choices: Le journaliste a été refusé l'entrée.
Le journaliste s'est vu refusé l'entrée.
Le journaliste s'est vu refuser l'entrée.
Le journaliste s'est vu à refuser l'entrée.
questions.explanation: Refuser quelque chose à quelqu'un: the journalist is an indirect object, so he can't be the subject of an ordinary passive. Se voir + infinitive solves it: il s'est vu refuser l'entrée. After se voir comes an infinitive (refuser), with no preposition.

questions.stem: Complete in standard written French: "Elle s'est ___ retirer son permis."
questions.explanation: She doesn't do the removing (others take her licence away), so se is not the direct object of voir: vu stays invariable. Compare elle s'est vue contrainte, where she is what is seen.

questions.stem: Complete: "Après le scandale, elle s'est ___ contrainte de démissionner."
questions.explanation: Se voir + participle describes the situation the subject finds herself in; se is the direct object of voir, so vue agrees with elle (feminine singular).

questions.stem: Complete in standard French: "Mon frère et ma sœur se sont ___ arrêter à la frontière."
questions.explanation: Fait followed by an infinitive never agrees: ils se sont fait arrêter. The agreed forms are seen in casual writing but are wrong in standard French.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "She let herself be persuaded"?
questions.explanation: Se laisser + infinitive = to let yourself be …: elle s'est laissé convaincre (laissé invariable under the 1990 rules, and correct under the older rule too, since others do the convincing). Without se, "elle a laissé convaincre" has no one being persuaded.

questions.stem: Complete the notice: "___ rappelé aux visiteurs que les photos sont interdites."
questions.explanation: An impersonal construction: the empty subject il and a singular verb, with the people after it (aux visiteurs). "Ils sont rappelés" would mean the visitors themselves are called back.

questions.stem: Which version would you expect in an official report?
choices: On a dit qu'on reportait l'audience, voilà.
Il a été décidé de reporter l'audience.
questions.explanation: The impersonal passive (il a été décidé de …) is the register of minutes and official texts. The others are spoken French: on, quoi, voilà and the dislocated "L'audience, ils l'ont reportée".

questions.stem: What does "Ce genre d'affaire se juge devant la cour d'assises" mean?
choices: This kind of case is tried before the criminal court.
This kind of case judges the criminal court.
A case like this was tried yesterday.
The court judges itself in this kind of case.
questions.explanation: A pronominal passive states a general rule: se juge = is tried. Its subject (ce genre d'affaire) undergoes the action.

questions.stem: In this lesson's simplified picture, which court tries a person for a délit such as theft?
questions.explanation: Délits are tried by the tribunal correctionnel, where the person is le prévenu. The cour d'assises tries crimes, the tribunal de police minor offences, and the Conseil constitutionnel checks laws, not people.

questions.stem: What is "une peine de deux ans avec sursis"?
choices: two years in prison, to be served
a fine equal to two years' salary
a two-year sentence that, as a rule, isn't served unless the person offends again
a two-year wait before the trial
questions.explanation: Avec sursis = suspended. A sentence to be served is une peine ferme.

questions.stem: Who is "le prévenu"?
choices: the person tried for a délit
questions.explanation: Le prévenu (la prévenue) is the person tried for a délit before the tribunal correctionnel. The person tried for a crime before the cour d'assises is l'accusé.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ceux qui ___ la loi seront poursuivis."
questions.explanation: Enfreindre conjugates like peindre: ils enfreignent (gn in the plural), participle enfreint.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct French?
choices: Je me suis vu demandé de témoigner.
questions.explanation: Demander à quelqu'un de …: the person is an indirect object, so no ordinary passive. Use on (on m'a demandé de …) or se voir + infinitive (je me suis vu demander de …, with the infinitive demander, not the participle).

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What did the lawyer announce?

audio.text: Le prévenu, poursuivi pour fraude, a été condamné hier à un an de prison avec sursis. Son avocat a annoncé qu'il ferait appel.

choices: that his client had been acquitted
that the trial had been postponed
that his client would go to prison
questions.explanation: Son avocat a annoncé qu'il ferait appel = his lawyer announced that he would appeal. The client was given a suspended sentence (avec sursis), so he isn't going to prison.

questions.stem: Listen to two people disagreeing. What does the second speaker think?

audio.text: Il s'est fait arrêter, c'est bien qu'il est coupable ! Pas du tout. Tant qu'il n'est pas jugé, il bénéficie de la présomption d'innocence.

choices: The man is guilty because he was arrested.
The man has already been tried and convicted.
The man should be released at once.
The man must be treated as innocent until he's tried.
questions.explanation: Tant qu'il n'est pas jugé, il bénéficie de la présomption d'innocence = as long as he hasn't been tried, he is presumed innocent.

questions.stem: Complete with one word (standard French): "Elle s'est ___ voler son téléphone dans le métro." (She had her phone stolen.)
questions.explanation: Se faire + infinitive for something unwelcome done to you: elle s'est fait voler son téléphone. Fait before an infinitive never agrees.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "He had his licence taken away."
questions.explanation: Il s'est vu retirer son permis: se voir + infinitive, with the object (son permis) after the infinitive.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its construction.
left: Il a été décidé que le procès aurait lieu en mai.
questions.explanation: Il a été décidé: empty il + passive. S'est vu refuser: se voir + infinitive. Ça ne se fait pas: a pronominal passive for a rule. A été condamné: être + participle. No sentence uses se laisser.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in standard written French? Select all that apply.
choices: Elle s'est vu refuser l'accès au tribunal.
Ils se sont fait condamner à une amende.
Il est interdit de filmer pendant l'audience.
Elle s'est faite arrêter hier soir.
Le témoin a été demandé de revenir.
questions.explanation: Vu stays invariable when others do the action (refuser), fait never agrees before an infinitive, and "il est interdit de" is the impersonal construction. "S'est faite arrêter" wrongly agrees fait; demander à quelqu'un has no ordinary passive (on a demandé au témoin de revenir).

questions.stem: Name the numbered people and places in this courtroom.

image.alt: A simplified courtroom with four numbered parts: a judge in a black robe at a raised bench, a man standing in a glass box next to a guard, a lawyer in a black robe behind a desk, and a woman speaking at a small stand with a microphone.

questions.explanation: 1 is the judge at the bench: le juge (la juge for a woman). 2 is in the dock, the glass box: l'accusé. 3 is the lawyer's desk: la défense. 4 speaks at the stand: le témoin. Le casier judiciaire is a record and le délit an offence, not people or places.

questions.stem: Complete: "Fatiguées ? Oui, elles ___ sont vraiment."
questions.explanation: Le neutre replaces an adjective used as an attribute, and it never agrees: elles le sont, even though fatiguées is feminine plural.

questions.stem: "Tu es sûr qu'il viendra ?" Which answer is correct?
questions.explanation: Être sûr de + an idea → en: j'en suis sûr. Y replaces à + an idea, and le can't stand for a de-complement here.

questions.stem: "Tu t'attendais à leur séparation ?" Which answer is correct?
choices: Non, je ne m'en attendais pas.
Non, je ne lui attendais pas.
Non, je ne m'y attendais pas.
Non, je ne la m'attendais pas.
questions.explanation: S'attendre à + an idea → y: je ne m'y attendais pas (I didn't expect it). En would need a verb with de, lui is for a person, and "la m'" breaks the pronoun order.

questions.stem: In careful written French, how do you replace "à mon frère" in "Je pense souvent à mon frère"?
questions.explanation: Penser à + a person takes à + a stressed pronoun in careful French: je pense à lui. "J'y pense" for a person is informal speech; "je lui pense" is wrong (penser à isn't an indirect-object verb), and "je le pense" means "I think so".

questions.stem: What does "Je lui en veux" mean?
choices: I want some from him (or her).
I hold it against him (or her).
questions.explanation: En vouloir à quelqu'un is an idiomatic pronominal verb: to be angry with someone, to hold something against them. It has nothing to do with wanting.

questions.stem: Complete: "Elle ne sait pas comment ___ pour lui annoncer la nouvelle."
questions.explanation: S'y prendre = to go about it: comment s'y prendre (how to go about it). S'en prendre à means to take it out on someone and needs à + a person; "se le prendre" and "y prendre" aren't used for this.

questions.stem: Complete in standard French: "Elle s'en est ___ de ne pas l'avoir écouté."
questions.explanation: In s'en vouloir, se is an indirect object (vouloir à soi), so the participle stays invariable: elle s'en est voulu. Compare elle s'en est prise à lui, which agrees.

questions.stem: Complete this general piece of advice: "Pour réussir un entretien, il faut avoir confiance en ___."
questions.explanation: After an impersonal subject (il faut, on, chacun), the stressed pronoun is soi: avoir confiance en soi. Se is never used after a preposition, eux is plural, and lui-même would point to a particular man.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses "autrui" correctly?
choices: Respecter la vie privée d'autrui est essentiel.
questions.explanation: Autrui (others, other people) is formal, normally takes no article and has no plural; it usually follows a preposition: la vie privée d'autrui.

questions.stem: "D'aucuns pensent que la vie à deux est dépassée." What does "d'aucuns" mean, and what is its register?
questions.explanation: D'aucuns = some people, a literary word, often a little ironic. Despite aucun, it isn't negative. Everyday French says certains.

questions.stem: "Leur rupture ? Je n'y suis pour rien." What does the speaker mean?
choices: I had nothing to do with it.
questions.explanation: N'y être pour rien = to have nothing to do with it; y être pour quelque chose = to have something to do with it.

questions.stem: Replace "ce secret" with a pronoun: "Il m'a confié ce secret."
questions.explanation: The order is me before le: il me l'a confié. Lui would replace a person, not the secret.

questions.stem: Listen to the voicemail. How does Nora feel?

audio.text: Salut, c'est Nora. Je sais que tu m'en veux pour samedi. Je m'y suis vraiment mal prise, et je m'en veux aussi. Rappelle-moi, j'y tiens.

choices: She is angry with her friend.
She doesn't care about the quarrel.
She blames herself and wants to make up.
questions.explanation: Je m'en veux = I blame myself; je m'y suis mal prise = I went about it badly; j'y tiens = it matters to me. Tu m'en veux is what her friend feels.

questions.stem: Listen. Why doesn't the second speaker believe they'll make up?

audio.text: Tu crois à leur réconciliation ? Franchement, non, je n'y crois pas. Elle est beaucoup trop rancunière.

choices: She is jealous of her sister.
questions.explanation: Elle est trop rancunière = she holds grudges too much. Je n'y crois pas: y stands for leur réconciliation (croire à).

questions.stem: Complete with one pronoun: "Cette dispute, tu y penses encore ? — Oui, j'___ pense tous les jours."
questions.explanation: Penser à + a thing or idea → y: j'y pense (I think about it). With a person, careful French would say je pense à lui / à elle.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I wasn't expecting it."
questions.explanation: Je ne m'y attendais pas. The pronouns (m', y) come right before the verb, inside ne … pas.

questions.stem: Match each verb to its meaning.
questions.explanation: These idiomatic pronominal verbs have to be learned whole. To break up is rompre, and to confide in is se confier à.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in standard written French? Select all that apply.
choices: Ils étaient amis, mais ils ne le sont plus.
Je pense à elle tous les jours.
questions.explanation: Neutral le stays le (ils ne le sont plus), penser à takes à + stressed pronoun (à elle), and s'y connaître en is correct. "Elle la est" should be elle l'est, and "je lui pense" should be je pense à lui.

questions.stem: Name the numbered stages of this couple's story.

image.alt: A timeline of a couple's story in seven stages, with five numbered: two people smiling side by side; the two inside a house; the two moving apart with a broken heart above; one person alone under a dark rain cloud; the two holding hands under a heart.

questions.explanation: 1, smiling together: la complicité. 2, sharing a home: la vie à deux. 3, moving apart: la rupture. 4, alone under a dark cloud: la rancune (resentment). 5, holding hands again: la réconciliation.

questions.stem: What does "le cas échéant" mean in "Le cas échéant, joignez une copie du jugement"?
questions.explanation: Le cas échéant = if the situation arises, where applicable. "In that case" is dans ce cas, "in any case" en tout cas, "at the latest" au plus tard.

questions.stem: A woman is writing a certificate. Complete: "Je ___ Claire Martin certifie que les informations ci-dessus sont exactes."
questions.explanation: Soussigné agrees with the writer: a woman writes je soussignée. Soussignés is plural, and soussignant isn't used.

questions.stem: What does "à compter du 1er mars" give?
questions.explanation: À compter de = as from: the date something starts. A deadline is au plus tard le … or avant le …

questions.stem: Complete the lease: "Le locataire peut ___ le bail à tout moment, sous réserve d'un préavis de trois mois."
questions.explanation: Résilier un contrat, un bail, un abonnement = to terminate it. Enfreindre is to break a law, promulguer is for laws, and déconnecter for the internet.

questions.stem: In "M. Diallo, ci-après dénommé « le Locataire »", what does "ci-après" tell you?
choices: He was mentioned earlier in the document.
From here on, the document calls him "the Tenant".
questions.explanation: Ci-après = hereafter, below in the document: from now on he is called "the Tenant". Ci-dessus would point to something earlier.

questions.stem: What does "Nonobstant toute clause contraire" mean?
choices: Despite any clause to the contrary
In accordance with the clause above
questions.explanation: Nonobstant is legalese for malgré: notwithstanding, despite. Sous réserve de = subject to; conformément à = in accordance with.

questions.stem: What does "ledit contrat" mean in everyday French?
questions.explanation: Ledit = le + dit, "the said": the contract already mentioned. It agrees like le: ladite clause, lesdits locataires.

questions.stem: The terms say: "À l'issue de cette période, l'abonnement est reconduit tacitement." What happens at the end of the first period?
choices: The membership renews only if you ask.
The membership renews automatically unless you cancel.
The membership renews at a lower price.
questions.explanation: Reconduit tacitement = renewed tacitly, without anyone saying anything: it goes on unless you cancel (résilier).

questions.stem: Which sentence suits a private person's cancellation letter?
choices: Nonobstant ledit article, je résilie susdit abonnement.
Conformément à l'article 9.2 de vos conditions générales, je souhaite résilier mon abonnement.
Il est résilié l'abonnement par moi.
questions.explanation: The formula conformément à + the article is clear and polite. Legalese (nonobstant, ledit) sounds strange from a private person, the informal note is the wrong register, and "il est résilié l'abonnement par moi" isn't French.

questions.stem: Complete with one word from the lesson: "___ à la loi, vos données ne seront pas transmises à des tiers." (In accordance with the law, …)
questions.explanation: Conformément à = in accordance with: conformément à la loi. (Des tiers: third parties.)

questions.stem: Match each formula to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Sous réserve de = subject to; en vertu de = by virtue of, under; à compter de = as from; ci-dessus = above. Notwithstanding is nonobstant and attached is ci-joint.

questions.stem: Which are typical of the administrative style? Select all that apply.
choices: nouns instead of verbs (la résiliation du contrat)
questions.explanation: Administrative French is nominal, impersonal and full of fixed formulas. Slang, abbreviations, exclamations and rhetorical questions belong to other registers.

questions.stem: Put the parts of this cancellation letter in order.
choices: Objet : résiliation de mon abonnement n° 48213
Je soussignée Clara Benoît vous informe de ma décision de résilier cet abonnement.
Je vous remercie de bien vouloir m'adresser une confirmation écrite.
Veuillez agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées.
questions.explanation: Subject line, greeting, the decision (with je soussignée), the request for confirmation, and the closing formula last.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this contract.

image.alt: The first page of an invented subscription contract with four numbered parts: a box with two names at the top, a shaded numbered article in the middle, a line with a town and a date at the bottom left, and a signature under the words Lu et approuvé at the bottom right.

questions.explanation: 1 names the parties who sign: les soussignés. 2 is one numbered provision: la clause. 3, Fait à Nantes, le 3 mars: the place and date. 4 is the signature, under Lu et approuvé. Le préavis is a notice period, and le bailleur is a landlord.

questions.topic: The institutions of the Fifth Republic
questions.stem: On what date was the Constitution of the Fifth Republic promulgated?
questions.explanation: The text was approved by referendum on 28 September 1958 and promulgated on 4 October 1958. The referendums of 1962 and 2000 changed how and for how long the president is elected.

questions.topic: The institutions of the Fifth Republic
questions.stem: Since which referendum has the president been elected by direct universal suffrage?
questions.explanation: The referendum of 28 October 1962 introduced election au suffrage universel direct; the first such election was held in December 1965 (an election, not a referendum).

questions.topic: The institutions of the Fifth Republic
questions.stem: What did the referendum of 24 September 2000 change?
choices: It introduced the direct election of the president.
The president's term went from seven years to five.
It limited presidents to two consecutive terms.
questions.explanation: The 2000 referendum created le quinquennat, first applied in 2002. The Conseil constitutionnel dates from 1958, direct election from 1962, and the two-term limit from a 2008 revision.

questions.topic: The institutions of the Fifth Republic
questions.stem: How are senators elected?
choices: they are appointed by the president
by indirect universal suffrage, through colleges of grands électeurs
they are chosen by the deputies
questions.explanation: Senators are elected au suffrage universel indirect by grands électeurs, mostly delegates of municipal councils, for six years.

questions.topic: The institutions of the Fifth Republic
questions.stem: How many deputies sit in the Assemblée nationale?
questions.explanation: The Assemblée nationale has 577 députés. 348 is the number of senators, 925 both chambers together, and 9 the members appointed to the Conseil constitutionnel.

questions.stem: Who promulgates a law, and within what time limit?
choices: the Prime Minister, within a month
the Conseil constitutionnel, within eight days
the president of the Sénat, within fifteen days
the president of the Republic, within fifteen days
questions.explanation: The president promulgue la loi within fifteen days of receiving the finally adopted text; then it is published in the Journal officiel.

questions.stem: What is "la navette"?
choices: the joint committee of seven deputies and seven senators
the text going back and forth between the two chambers
a vote that can bring down the government
a referral to the Conseil constitutionnel
questions.explanation: La navette (literally "the shuttle") is the back-and-forth of a bill between the Assemblée and the Sénat until both vote the same text. If they still disagree, a commission mixte paritaire may meet.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written in the formal style of this lesson?
choices: Les députés, ils ont voté la loi, et puis le président l'a signée.
Adoptée par l'Assemblée nationale, la loi a été promulguée le 3 mars.
On a voté la loi, et voilà.
La loi, c'est bon, elle est passée.
questions.explanation: The formal version opens with a passive participle (adoptée par …) and uses the passive (a été promulguée). The others are spoken French: dislocation, on, voilà, c'est bon.

questions.topic: The institutions of the Fifth Republic
questions.stem: Who can refer a law to the Conseil constitutionnel before it is promulgated?
choices: any citizen, by writing to it
only the president of the Republic
only the Sénat, by a majority vote
among others, sixty deputies or sixty senators
questions.explanation: Before promulgation, the president, the Prime Minister, the presidents of the two chambers, or sixty deputies or sixty senators can refer a law. Citizens can raise a QPC only during a court case, after the law is in force.

questions.topic: The institutions of the Fifth Republic
questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Le ___ est le mandat présidentiel de cinq ans."
questions.explanation: Le quinquennat (five-year term) replaced le septennat (seven-year term) after the referendum of 2000.

questions.stem: Put the stages of a law in order (simplified).
choices: Dépôt d'un projet ou d'une proposition de loi
Examen et vote dans les deux chambres (la navette)
Promulgation par le président de la République
questions.explanation: A bill is tabled, examined and voted by both chambers, possibly referred to the Conseil constitutionnel, promulgated by the president, then published in the Journal officiel. Notice the nominal style: dépôt, examen, saisine, promulgation, publication.

questions.topic: The institutions of the Fifth Republic
questions.stem: Match each number to what it counts.
choices: appointed members of the Conseil constitutionnel
questions.explanation: 577 deputies, 348 senators, 9 appointed members of the Conseil constitutionnel (former presidents sit by right in addition), and a six-year term for senators.

questions.topic: The institutions of the Fifth Republic
questions.stem: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
choices: Senators are elected for six years.
Half the Sénat is renewed every three years.
A president can serve any number of consecutive terms.
Former presidents of the Republic are members of the Conseil constitutionnel by right.
Deputies are elected by indirect suffrage.
questions.explanation: Senators serve six years, and half the seats are renewed every three years; former presidents sit on the Conseil constitutionnel by right. Since 2008 no one may serve more than two consecutive terms, and deputies are elected by direct suffrage.

questions.topic: The institutions of the Fifth Republic
questions.stem: In Switzerland, what is "une votation"?
choices: a popular vote on a question
questions.explanation: Une votation is a Swiss popular vote on a question (la votation populaire). The head of a Belgian commune is le bourgmestre.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il faut isoler les vieux logements, ___ le prix du chauffage augmente."
questions.explanation: "D'autant que" adds a strong extra reason (especially as the price is going up) and takes the indicative. "Non que" would reject the reason, with the real one following after "mais"; "au point que" and "si bien que" give a result, and insulating doesn't make the price of heating go up.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je n'ai pas pris d'abonnement, ___ ce soit cher, mais je n'en ai pas besoin."
questions.explanation: The speaker sets a reason aside (it isn't the price) and gives the real one after "mais". That is "non que", which takes the subjunctive: "ce soit". The other three take the indicative, and none of them rejects a cause.

questions.stem: Complete: "Non qu'il ___ contre le projet, mais il veut des garanties."
questions.explanation: "Non que" presents a cause only to reject it, so the verb is in the subjunctive: "qu'il soit". "Est", "sera" and "a été" are indicative forms, which would present the reason as true.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly gives the reason for the conviction?
choices: Il a été condamné pour frauder.
Il a été condamné pour fraudant.
Il a été condamné de frauder.
Il a été condamné pour avoir fraudé.
questions.explanation: After verbs of judging (condamner, punir, féliciter, remercier), the reason is "pour" + past infinitive: "pour avoir fraudé", because the fraud came first. "Pour frauder" would mean "in order to commit fraud"; "pour fraudant" and "de frauder" aren't French.

questions.stem: What does this formal sentence mean? "Le budget manquait. Aussi le projet a-t-il été reporté."
choices: The money wasn't there, and so the project was postponed.
The money wasn't there, and the project was also postponed.
The money wasn't there; even so, the project was postponed.
The money wasn't there. Was the project postponed too?
questions.explanation: At the start of a formal sentence, "aussi" + inversion ("le projet a-t-il") means "and so, therefore". It doesn't mean "also" there, and the inversion doesn't make it a question: it's the complex inversion of careful writing.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ces difficultés ___ d'un choix fait il y a quarante ans."
questions.explanation: The effect is the subject and the cause follows "de": "découler de" (to follow from). "Engendrer", "susciter" and "déclencher" go the other way (cause → effect) and take a direct object, not "de".

questions.stem: Complete: "Le projet d'éoliennes a ___ un vif débat dans le village."
questions.explanation: "Susciter" (to arouse, to give rise to) takes a direct object and suits reactions and debates: "susciter un débat". "Découler" and "résulter" need "de" + the cause and are used with the effect as subject; "aboutir" needs "à".

questions.stem: Which connector belongs in a formal report rather than in conversation?
questions.explanation: "Compte tenu de" (given, considering) is formal: "Compte tenu de la hausse des prix, …". "Du coup" and "vu que" are typical of speech, and "histoire de" (lesson 18) is informal.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il a réduit son chauffage ___ avoir froid chez lui."
questions.explanation: The subject is the same (il … il), so the infinitive is needed: "au point de" + infinitive, elided before "avoir": "au point d'avoir froid". "Au point que" and "à tel point que" need a full clause with its own verb, and "d'autant que" gives a cause.

questions.stem: What does "Du moment que tu es d'accord, je signe" mean?
choices: Until you agree, I won't sign.
At the moment you agree, sign.
Even though you agree, I'll sign.
questions.explanation: "Du moment que" + indicative means "since, given that" (often "as long as"). It isn't about time ("until", "at the moment"), and it doesn't concede anything ("even though" would be "bien que" or "même si").

questions.stem: Read: "À la suite d'une panne sur une ligne à haute tension, trois départements ont été privés d'électricité pendant deux heures. La coupure a déclenché la colère des commerçants, d'autant que c'était la troisième en un mois. Non que le réseau soit en mauvais état, assure l'opérateur, mais les orages de juin ont été exceptionnels." According to the operator, why have there been so many power cuts?
choices: Because the grid is in poor condition.
Because the shopkeepers used too much power.
Because the June storms were exceptional.
Because three departments share one line.
questions.explanation: The operator rejects one cause with "Non que le réseau soit en mauvais état" (not that the grid is in poor condition) and gives the real one after "mais": the June storms were exceptional. The shopkeepers' anger is a consequence ("a déclenché la colère"), not a cause.

questions.stem: Listen to the news flash. What are people asked to do?

audio.text: Flash info. À la suite de la vague de froid, la consommation d'électricité a atteint hier soir un niveau record. Le gestionnaire du réseau appelle les Français à réduire leur consommation entre dix-huit et vingt heures, afin d'éviter toute coupure.

choices: Stay at home during the cold snap.
Switch off their heating all evening.
Report power cuts to the grid operator.
Use less electricity between 6 and 8 pm.
questions.explanation: The flash says that, following the cold snap, consumption hit a record, and the grid operator "appelle les Français à réduire leur consommation entre dix-huit et vingt heures": to cut consumption between 6 and 8 pm, to avoid power cuts. Nobody is asked to stay in, to switch heating off all evening or to report cuts.

questions.stem: Listen to the two neighbours. What does the first speaker object to?

audio.text: — Ces éoliennes, franchement, elles vont gâcher le paysage. — Peut-être, mais elles produisent de l'électricité sans charbon ni pétrole, d'autant que chez nous, le vent ne manque pas. — Non que je sois contre les renouvelables, mais pourquoi juste devant chez moi ?

choices: Where the wind turbines will stand.
The noise of the turbines at night.
The cost of the project for taxpayers.
questions.explanation: He says "Non que je sois contre les renouvelables": he rejects the idea that he opposes renewables in general. His real complaint is the place: "pourquoi juste devant chez moi ?" (why right in front of my house?). Noise and cost aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: Complete in a formal style: "Les prix ont doublé en un an ; ___ la colère des usagers."
questions.explanation: "De là" + noun gives the consequence in a few words: hence the users' anger. The other three need a full clause with a verb: "d'autant que" and "non que" introduce causes, "au point que" a result clause.

questions.stem: Complete with the present of "résulter": "Il en ___ que la facture d'électricité va augmenter."
questions.explanation: "Il en résulte que" + indicative = as a result, it follows that. "Résulter" is used in the third person; here it's impersonal, with "il".

questions.stem: Complete with a connector meaning "to the point that" (two or more words): "Le vent a soufflé ___ les éoliennes ont dû être arrêtées."
questions.explanation: "Au point que" or the slightly stronger "à tel point que" + indicative: the wind blew so hard that the turbines had to be stopped.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to write, in a formal style: "And so the project was put off."
questions.explanation: Aussi le projet a-t-il été reporté. At the start of a formal sentence, "aussi" (and so) is followed by complex inversion: the noun subject stays first, and "il" is added after the auxiliary.

questions.stem: Match each connector with what follows it.
questions.explanation: "D'autant que" + indicative (an extra reason); "non que" + subjunctive (a rejected reason); "compte tenu de" + noun (given); "au point de" + infinitive when the subject is the same.

questions.stem: Which of these are followed by the indicative? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "D'autant que", "du moment que" and "à tel point que" introduce facts, so they take the indicative. "Non que" and its spoken form "ce n'est pas que" reject a cause and take the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the picture.

image.alt: A landscape with four numbered markers: on a wind turbine on a hill, on a cooling tower of a power station, on the solar panels on a house roof, and on the cables between two pylons.

questions.explanation: 1 l'éolienne (wind turbine), 2 la centrale (power station, here nuclear, with its cooling towers), 3 le panneau solaire (solar panel), 4 le réseau électrique (the grid: pylons and cables). "Le combustible" (fuel) and "la pénurie" (shortage) aren't objects in the picture.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je pars tôt ___ rater le train."
questions.explanation: The subject is the same (je pars, je rate), so use a preposition + infinitive: "de peur de rater le train" (for fear of missing the train). "De peur que" and "pour que" need a clause with a subjunctive; "loin de rater" would mean "far from missing".

questions.stem: In careful written French: "Je pars tôt, de peur que le train ___ complet."
questions.explanation: "De peur que" takes the subjunctive, often with the optional ne explétif in careful style: "de peur que le train ne soit complet". "N'est", "ne sera" and "ne serait" are indicative or conditionnel forms.

questions.stem: What does "Prends un parapluie, de peur qu'il ne pleuve" mean?
choices: Take an umbrella in case it rains.
Take an umbrella in case it doesn't rain.
Take an umbrella because it isn't raining.
Take an umbrella although it's raining.
questions.explanation: The "ne" after "de peur que" is the optional ne explétif, not a negative: the fear is that it will rain. "In case it doesn't rain" would need "ne … pas": "de peur qu'il ne pleuve pas".

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: La gare a été rénovée dans le but des Jeux olympiques.
La gare a été rénovée en vue des Jeux olympiques.
La gare a été rénovée de façon aux Jeux olympiques.
La gare a été rénovée afin des Jeux olympiques.
questions.explanation: "En vue de" takes a noun (or an infinitive): "en vue des Jeux" (with a view to the Games). "Dans le but de", "de façon à" and "afin de" are followed by an infinitive, not by a noun like this.

questions.stem: The sentence expresses a purpose. Complete: "Parle plus fort, de sorte que tout le monde t'___."
questions.explanation: For a purpose (so that everyone hears you), "de sorte que" takes the subjunctive: "t'entende". With the indicative ("t'entend") it would state a result, which doesn't fit after an order.

questions.stem: In "Les horaires ont été revus, de sorte que les usagers peuvent désormais prendre le train de 8 h", what does "de sorte que" express?
questions.explanation: "Peuvent" is indicative (the subjunctive would be "puissent"), so "de sorte que" states a result: the timetables were revised, and as a result passengers can now take the 8 o'clock train.

questions.stem: What does "Loin de se plaindre, les usagers ont applaudi la nouvelle ligne" mean?
choices: Far from complaining, the passengers applauded the new line.
Living far away, the passengers applauded the new line.
Without complaining much, the passengers applauded the new line.
The passengers complained before applauding the new line.
questions.explanation: "Loin de" + infinitive sets what happened against what you might expect: instead of complaining, they applauded. It has nothing to do with distance here.

questions.stem: In "Si le train est plus lent que l'avion, il est aussi plus confortable", what does "si" mean?
questions.explanation: This is the "si" of contrast: both facts are true (the train is slower, and it's more comfortable), and the second clause answers the first. It isn't a condition.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il a eu une promotion, mais il n'est pas plus heureux ___."
questions.explanation: "Pour autant" (for all that) says that the promotion didn't lead to the result you'd expect. "Quitte à", "de peur de" and "en vue de" all need an infinitive or a noun after them.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je prends le train, ___ arriver une heure plus tard qu'en voiture."
questions.explanation: "Quitte à" + infinitive accepts a cost for a choice: I'm taking the train, even if it means arriving an hour later. Taking the train "for fear of" or "with the aim of" arriving later makes no sense.

questions.stem: Which expression is informal?
questions.explanation: "Histoire de" + infinitive (On sort, histoire de prendre l'air) is casual speech. "Afin de" is neutral to formal; "dans le but de" and "en vue de" are formal.

questions.stem: Read: "Pour rompre l'isolement du plateau, le département a lancé une navette à la demande. Loin de rouler à vide, elle transporte une centaine d'usagers par semaine. Le service reste toutefois coûteux, si bien que son avenir n'est pas garanti." Which statement is true?
choices: The shuttle often runs empty, so it will stop.
The shuttle is well used, but its cost puts its future in doubt.
The shuttle is cheap, so its future is secure.
The shuttle was launched to reduce traffic in town.
questions.explanation: "Loin de rouler à vide" means it does not run empty: it carries about a hundred passengers a week. But it is "coûteux" (costly), "si bien que son avenir n'est pas garanti" (so its future isn't guaranteed). Its aim was to break the isolation of the plateau, not to reduce town traffic.

questions.stem: Listen to the voicemail. What is Lucie going to do?

audio.text: Bonjour, c'est Lucie. Je t'appelle de la gare : mon train est supprimé à cause d'un incident sur la voie. Je vais prendre la navette jusqu'à Valence, quitte à arriver avec une heure de retard. Ne m'attends pas pour dîner !

choices: Wait at the station for the next train.
Cancel her trip and come home.
Take the shuttle to Valence and arrive about an hour late.
Take a taxi so as not to be late for dinner.
questions.explanation: Her train is cancelled, so she'll take the shuttle to Valence, "quitte à arriver avec une heure de retard" (even if it means arriving an hour late), and she says not to wait for her for dinner.

questions.stem: Listen to the traffic news. Why are drivers asked to leave the motorway earlier tonight?

audio.text: Info trafic. En raison de travaux, le péage de Montclair sera fermé cette nuit de 22 heures à 5 heures. Les automobilistes sont invités à sortir de l'autoroute avant, de façon à éviter les bouchons. Dans le sens Paris-province, la circulation est fluide.

choices: Because the motorway will be closed all day.
Because traffic towards Paris is very heavy.
Because the toll will be free tonight.
Because the toll will be closed from 10 pm to 5 am.
questions.explanation: The toll is closed overnight for roadworks ("sera fermé cette nuit de 22 heures à 5 heures"), and drivers are asked to leave earlier "de façon à éviter les bouchons" (so as to avoid jams). Traffic towards the provinces is said to be flowing freely.

questions.stem: Complete with the two-word expression meaning "even if it means": "Je prends le vélo, ___ arriver mouillé."
questions.explanation: "Quitte à" + infinitive: I'm taking the bike, even if it means arriving wet.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "___ de se plaindre, il a remercié tout le monde." (Far from complaining, he thanked everyone.)
questions.explanation: "Loin de" + infinitive: far from complaining. It opposes what happened to what you'd expect.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Park so as not to block the exit."
questions.explanation: Garez-vous de manière à ne pas gêner la sortie. "De manière à" + infinitive, with "ne pas" together before the infinitive.

questions.stem: Match each connector with what follows it.
questions.explanation: "De peur que" + subjunctive (different subjects); "de peur de" + infinitive (same subject); "en vue de" + noun or infinitive (en vue des Jeux, en vue d'obtenir); "pour autant" is an adverb (il n'est pas plus heureux pour autant).

questions.stem: Which sentences express a purpose? Select all that apply.
choices: Je pars tôt de peur de rater le train.
La ville a créé des voies de bus dans le but de réduire les bouchons.
Loin de se plaindre, il a applaudi.
Si le train est lent, il est confortable.
On sort, histoire de prendre l'air.
questions.explanation: "De peur de", "dans le but de" and "histoire de" (informal) give the aim of an action. "Loin de" and the "si" of contrast set two facts against each other: they express opposition.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the picture.

image.alt: A rural landscape with five numbered markers: on a toll booth across a motorway, on a container wagon of a train, on a minibus outside a small station, on a green post with a car plugged into it, and on a kick scooter ridden on a cycle path.

questions.explanation: 1 le péage (the toll booths across the motorway), 2 le fret (the freight train of containers), 3 la navette (the shuttle minibus at the station), 4 la borne de recharge (the charging point), 5 la trottinette (the kick scooter). There's no traffic jam (le bouchon) and no metro (le métro) in the picture.

questions.stem: The director said: « Partez ! » Complete: "Le directeur a exigé que nous ___."
questions.explanation: A verb of will (exiger que) takes the subjunctive, and in modern French it stays in the present even after a past verb: "que nous partions". "Partons" is indicative, "partirions" conditionnel, and "partir" can't follow "que".

questions.stem: In careful written French: "Elle déplore que la bibliothèque ___ fermée le dimanche."
questions.explanation: "Déplorer que" expresses a feeling (regret, criticism), so careful French uses the subjunctive: "soit". "Est", "sera" and "était" are indicative.

questions.stem: Which verb shows that the speaker gave way on a point to the other side?
questions.explanation: "Concéder" means to concede, to admit a point to an opponent: Il a concédé que le budget était trop élevé. "Rétorquer" is to answer back sharply, "insinuer" to suggest something unpleasant indirectly, "éluder" to dodge a question.

questions.stem: Complete: "Interrogé sur le coût, l'adjoint a ___ la question."
questions.explanation: "Éluder une question" = to dodge it, to avoid answering. You can't "garantir", "déplorer" or "insinuer" a question in this sense.

questions.stem: Complete: "L'association a mis en garde ___ une hausse des impôts locaux."
questions.explanation: "Mettre en garde contre" + noun = to warn against: mettre en garde contre une hausse des impôts. The noun is "la mise en garde".

questions.stem: A journalist writes: "À en croire le maire, tout le monde serait d'accord." What does the journalist suggest?
choices: She confirms what the mayor says.
She doubts what the mayor says.
She is quoting her own opinion.
questions.explanation: "À en croire" (if X is to be believed) signals doubt, and the conditionnel "serait" marks the information as unconfirmed. Together they put distance between the journalist and the mayor's claim.

questions.stem: Which expression signals clear doubt about a source?
questions.explanation: "À en croire la mairie" means "if the town hall is to be believed": the writer isn't convinced. "Selon" and "d'après" attribute neutrally, and "comme l'indique" even supports the source.

questions.stem: What does "L'opposition a insinué que la décision avait été prise avant la réunion" mean?
choices: The opposition proved that the decision had been made before the meeting.
The opposition denied that the decision had been made before the meeting.
The opposition regretted that the decision had been made before the meeting.
The opposition hinted, without saying it openly, that the decision had been made before the meeting.
questions.explanation: "Insinuer que" + indicative = to suggest something unpleasant indirectly. Proving would be "prouver", denying "nier", regretting "déplorer".

questions.stem: Which sentence is in free indirect speech?
choices: Il ne démissionnerait pas : il avait été élu pour cinq ans, et il irait jusqu'au bout !
Il a déclaré qu'il ne démissionnerait pas.
Il a déclaré : « Je ne démissionnerai pas. »
Selon lui, il ne démissionnera pas.
questions.explanation: Free indirect speech gives the minister's view in narrative tenses (conditionnel, plus-que-parfait) with no reporting verb, no "que" and no quotation marks, and keeps his voice (the exclamation). "Il a déclaré qu'il …" is indirect speech, the version in « » is direct speech, and "Selon lui" is a plain attribution.

questions.stem: This free indirect speech comes from a novel: "Elle partirait demain. Elle ne pouvait plus rester ici !" Which is the same thought in direct speech?
choices: « Je partirais demain. Je ne pouvais plus rester ici ! »
« Je partirai demain. Je ne peux plus rester ici ! »
« Elle partira demain. Elle ne peut plus rester ici ! »
« Je suis partie hier. Je ne pouvais plus rester ici ! »
questions.explanation: To go back to direct speech, use the first person and move each tense one step towards the present: conditionnel → futur (partirai), imparfait → présent (peux). Keeping "partirais" and "pouvais" forgets the tense change; "elle" forgets the person; "je suis partie hier" changes the meaning.

questions.stem: The mayor spoke for ten minutes to say that he regretted the decision and thought it was a bad one. Which sentence sums it up best for a press review?
choices: Le maire s'est félicité de la décision.
Le maire a éludé la décision.
Le maire a déploré la décision.
Le maire a garanti la décision.
questions.explanation: "Déplorer" (to regret publicly, to criticise) sums up the whole statement in one verb. "Se féliciter de" would mean he welcomed it; you can't "éluder" or "garantir" a decision in this sense.

questions.stem: In careful written French: "La ministre se félicite que le chômage ___ baissé."
questions.explanation: "Se féliciter que" expresses a feeling (being pleased), so careful French uses the subjunctive; the fall has already happened, so the past subjunctive: "ait baissé". "A, aura, avait" are indicative forms.

questions.stem: Listen to the interview. How does the mayor deal with the question?
